| `name` | Identifier, at most 63 characters. Required. |
| `check` | Lookups that must hold for every row, as an object or `Q(...)`. Values must be plain JSON or `F('field')`. No relation paths, no subqueries, no `Exists`. |
| `fields` | Unique columns (UniqueConstraint). |
| `condition` | Makes the unique constraint partial (only rows matching it). |

## The Model object

```ts
interface Model<F, T = Row<F>> {
  readonly name: string
  readonly fields: F
  readonly meta: ModelMeta
  readonly schema: z.ZodType<T>          // what a read returns
  readonly objects: QuerySet<T>          // see queryset.md
  create(data: Create<F>): Promise<T>
  get(id: string | number): Promise<T | undefined>
  update(id: string | number, patch: Partial<Record<keyof T & string, unknown>>): Promise<T>
  delete(id: string | number): Promise<void>
  related(name: string, id: string | number): RelatedManager
}
```

| Member | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `create(data)` | Validates `data` with a strict zod schema (unknown keys are refused), fills defaults (`uuid` pk = random UUID, `auto` / `autoNowAdd` / `autoNow` date/datetime = now, `default`), inserts, returns the stored row. Bad input → `DomainError('invalid_param')` naming the field. |
| `get(id)` | The row with that primary key, or `undefined`. |
| `update(id, patch)` | Writes `patch` (validated per field), sets every `autoNow` field not in the patch to now, re-reads and returns the row. Throws `DomainError('domain', '<model> <id> not found')` if no row matched. An empty patch still counts as a save. |
| `delete(id)` | Deletes that row (no error if it does not exist). `onDelete` rules apply. |
| `related(name, id)` | Manager for a many-to-many field or a reverse relation of row `id` (below). |
| `schema` | zod object of the row shape (keys use the stored name: `customerId` for fk `customer`). |

### Row and create types

```ts
type Row<F>    // what reads return
type Create<F> // what create() takes
type Infer<M>  // Row of a model: Infer<typeof Product>
```

- Row keys: the field name, except an fk field `customer` is stored and returned as `customerId`; m2m fields have no key.
- An `optional: true` field has type `V | null`.
- In `Create<F>`, a field is optional when it is `optional`, has `default`, `auto`, `autoNow`, `autoNowAdd`, or is `id` / `uuid`.

```ts
export const Product = defineModel('product', { id: field.id(), name: field.text() })
export type Product = Infer<typeof Product>   // { id: number; name: string }
```

### Errors from the database

Constraint failures come back in model vocabulary (`engine.ts wrapErr`), on every engine:

| Database error | DomainError |
|---|---|
| unique / primary key | `'domain'`, `"<model>.<field> must be unique"`, `field` set |
| not null / no default | `'invalid_param'`, `"<model>.<field> is required"` |
| foreign key | `'domain'`, `"<model> is still referenced by other records, or points at a record that does not exist"` |
| value too long / out of range (mysql) | `'invalid_param'`, `"<model>.<field> is too long or invalid"` |

## Relations

| Kind | Declared as | Column | Reverse accessor on the target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Foreign key (many-to-one) | `field.fk(() => Target, opts)` | `<name>Id` | `relatedName`, default `<sourceModelName>_set` |
| One-to-one | `field.fk(() => Target, { unique: true })` | `<name>Id UNIQUE` | same as fk |
| Many-to-many | `field.m2m(() => Target, { through?, relatedName? })` | none; a through table | `relatedName`, default `<sourceModelName>_set` |

The target is a function so models can point at each other before both are defined.

### onDelete (fk only)

| Value | What happens when the target row is deleted |
|---|---|
| `'RESTRICT'` (default) | The database refuses the delete. |
| `'PROTECT'` | The ORM checks first and throws `DomainError('domain', 'cannot delete <model>: still referenced by <source>.<field> (on delete PROTECT)')`; the database also has RESTRICT. |
| `'CASCADE'` | Referencing rows are deleted too. |
| `'SET_NULL'` | The fk becomes NULL. Needs `optional: true`. |
| `'SET_DEFAULT'` | The fk becomes its `default`. Needs `default`. On MySQL the ORM sets it before deleting. |
| `'DO_NOTHING'` | `NO ACTION` in the database. |

### Many-to-many

- Without `through`: an auto table named `<model>_<field>` (shortened if over 63 chars) with `id`, `<model>Id`, `<target>Id`, both `CASCADE`, unique per pair. A self-referencing m2m uses `from_<model>Id` / `to_<model>Id`.
- With `through: () => ThroughModel`: your model, which must have one fk to each side. Its rows are created / deleted through its own `objects`; `related(...).add/remove/set/clear` refuse.

### Reverse names and clashes

Every reverse name on a model must be unique and must not equal one of its field names. A clash throws at `defineModel` time: `"<A>.<f> and <B>.<g> both give <T> the reverse name "<n>": set relatedName on one of them"`.

### RelatedManager (`Model.related(name, id)`)

```ts
interface RelatedManager<T> {
  all(): QuerySet<T>
  add(...items: (string | number | object)[]): Promise<void>
  remove(...items: (string | number | object)[]): Promise<void>
  set(items: (string | number | object)[]): Promise<void>
  clear(): Promise<void>
}
```

| Relation | `all()` | `add / remove / set / clear` |
|---|---|---|
| m2m (either direction), auto through | the related rows | add missing pairs / delete pairs / make the set exactly this / delete all pairs. Each runs in `atomic()`. Items are ids or rows (the row's pk is used). |
| m2m with custom `through` | the related rows | refused (`invalid_param`): write the through model |
| reverse fk (`orders`, `order_set`) | the referencing rows | refused: set the fk on those rows instead |
| forward fk | refused: read the fk with `get()` | refused |

## Registry and discovery

- `modelRegistry(): Model[]` — every defined model. The last definition per name wins.
- `discoverModels(appsDir)` (used by `makemigrations`, `migrate`, `tvine shell`, `dumpdata`, `loaddata`) imports `apps/<app>/models.ts` for each installed app. A model belongs to the app whose `models.ts` exports it. Exporting the same model from two apps throws. Finding no models at all throws (so a broken import is never read as "all models removed").
- Defining or importing a model opens no database connection; the connection is looked up when a query runs.

## Swappable user model

`settings.auth.userModel`, default `'auth.User'` (table `auth_user`). A custom value `'accounts.User'` means table `accounts_user`, defined with `defineUserModel` / `extendUser` from `tvine/auth` in `apps/accounts/models.ts`. It must be chosen before the first `tvine migrate`; changing it later makes `migrate` fail with a checksum message. Details: [contrib/auth.md](contrib/auth.md).

## Examples

```ts
// apps/shop/models.ts
import { defineModel, field, CheckConstraint, type Infer } from 'tvine'

export const Customer = defineModel('customer', {
  id: field.id(),
  email: field.email({ unique: true }),
  name: field.text({ searchable: true }),
  joinedAt: field.datetime({ autoNowAdd: true }),
})

export const Tag = defineModel('tag', {
  id: field.id(),
  name: field.slug({ unique: true }),
})

export const Product = defineModel('product', {
  id: field.id(),
  sku: field.text({ unique: true }),
  name: field.text({ searchable: true }),
  price: field.money(),
  stock: field.int({ default: 0 }),
  active: field.bool({ default: true }),
  tags: field.m2m(() => Tag, { relatedName: 'products' }),
  updatedAt: field.datetime({ autoNow: true }),
}, { ordering: ['name'], indexes: [['active', 'name']] })

export const Order = defineModel('order', {
  id: field.id(),
  customer: field.fk(() => Customer, { onDelete: 'PROTECT', relatedName: 'orders' }),
  status: field.enum(['cart', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled'], { default: 'cart' }),
  total: field.money({ default: { value: 0, currency: 'USD' } }),
  createdAt: field.datetime({ autoNowAdd: true }),
}, { ordering: ['-createdAt'] })

export const OrderItem = defineModel('order_item', {
  id: field.id(),
  order: field.fk(() => Order, { onDelete: 'CASCADE', relatedName: 'items' }),
  product: field.fk(() => Product, { onDelete: 'PROTECT' }),
  quantity: field.int(),
}, {
  unique: [['order', 'product']],
  constraints: [CheckConstraint({ name: 'order_item_qty_positive', check: { quantity__gt: 0 } })],
})

export type Customer = Infer<typeof Customer>
export type Product = Infer<typeof Product>
export type Order = Infer<typeof Order>
```

Create, read, update, delete:

```ts
const ada = await Customer.create({ email: 'ada@example.com', name: 'Ada' })
const lamp = await Product.create({ sku: 'LAMP-1', name: 'Desk lamp', price: { value: 29.99, currency: 'USD' } })
const order = await Order.create({ customerId: ada.id })          // fk is passed as customerId
await OrderItem.create({ orderId: order.id, productId: lamp.id, quantity: 2 })

const same = await Product.get(lamp.id)                           // Product | undefined
await Product.update(lamp.id, { stock: 10 })                      // updatedAt set to now
await Order.delete(order.id)                                      // its items go too (CASCADE)
```

Many-to-many:

```ts
const desk = await Tag.create({ name: 'desk' })
await Product.related('tags', lamp.id).add(desk.id)
const tags = await Product.related('tags', lamp.id).all().all()   // QuerySet → rows
const lamps = await Tag.related('products', desk.id).all().all()  // reverse m2m by relatedName
await Product.related('tags', lamp.id).set([])                    // remove every tag
```

Reverse fk:

```ts
const adasOrders = await Customer.related('orders', ada.id).all().filter({ status: 'paid' }).all()
```

## Gotchas

- The fk key differs between definition and data: define `customer: field.fk(...)`, write and read `customerId`. Filters and `update()` accept both `customer` and `customerId`.
- `create()` refuses unknown keys, including m2m field names. Set m2m links with `related(...).add()` after creating.
- `Model.update()` sets `autoNow` fields; `Model.objects.filter(...).update()` does not.
- `get()` returns `undefined`, it does not throw. `update()` throws when the row is missing. `delete()` is silent.
- Rows are plain objects. There are no instance methods and no `save()`. (The user model gets methods such as `checkPassword` through an internal row prototype; app models cannot.)
- `default` must be a constant (it is written into the table DDL). There is no callable default; use `auto` / `autoNow` / `autoNowAdd` for timestamps, and a `uuid` pk is generated automatically.
- There is no separate one-to-one field: use `field.fk(..., { unique: true })`. Its reverse side is still a reverse fk (a list via `related()` / `prefetchRelated`), not a single object.
- `PROTECT` and `RESTRICT` both block deletes; only `PROTECT` gives the readable ORM error.

Not covered by the code (do not look for them): abstract models, model inheritance, proxy models, custom managers, verbose names / plural names, a `db_table` option (the name is the table), and model-level `clean()` validation.

## See also

- [fields.md](fields.md) — every field kind and option
- [queryset.md](queryset.md) — `objects`, lookups, relation spanning, prefetch
- [migrations.md](migrations.md) — turning models into tables
- [database.md](database.md) — connections and engines
- [contrib/auth.md](contrib/auth.md) — user model, `defineUserModel`, privacy export / erase
- [overview.md](overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/fields.md

# Fields

A field describes one model attribute: its JavaScript value type, how it is validated (zod), which column(s) it gets on each database, how values travel to and from the driver, and which filters it supports. You build fields with `field.<kind>(opts)` inside `defineModel`. Every field object in `warp/src/data/fields/*` owns its own DDL and conversion; the table only collects them. Source: `warp/src/data/fields.ts`, `warp/src/data/fields/*.ts`; admin widgets from `warp/src/contrib/admin/meta.ts`.

## Import

```ts
import { defineModel, field, inc, dec } from 'tvine'
```

In migration files use the `field` exported by `tvine/migrations` (same kinds; `fk` / `m2m` take a model name string). See [migrations.md](migrations.md).

## All kinds at a glance

| Builder | Kind | JS value | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field.id()` | `id` | `number` | 1, auto-increment pk |
| `field.uuid(o)` | `uuid` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.text(o)` | `text` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.int(o)` | `int` | `number` (integer) | 1 |
| `field.float(o)` | `float` | `number` | 1 |
| `field.bool(o)` | `bool` | `boolean` | 1 |
| `field.money(o)` | `money` | `{ value: number; currency: string }` | 2: `<name>`, `<name>Currency` |
| `field.enum(values, o)` | `enum` | one of `values` | 1 |
| `field.datetime(o)` | `datetime` | `Date` | 1 |
| `field.date(o)` | `date` | `'YYYY-MM-DD'` | 1 |
| `field.time(o)` | `time` | `'HH:MM:SS'` or `'HH:MM:SS.ffffff'` | 1 |
| `field.duration(o)` | `duration` | `number` (milliseconds) | 1 |
| `field.decimal(o)` | `decimal` | `string` (`'12.50'`) | 1 |
| `field.email(o)` | `email` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.url(o)` | `url` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.slug(o)` | `slug` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.file(o)` | `file` | `string` (storage key) | 1 |
| `field.image(o)` | `image` | `string` (storage key) | 1 |
| `field.signature(o)` | `image` | `string` (storage key) | 1 |
| `field.json(o)` | `json` | `unknown` | 1 |
| `field.color(o)` | `color` | `string` (`'#1a2b3c'`) | 1 |
| `field.phone(o)` | `phone` | `string` (E.164) | 1 |
| `field.ip(o)` | `ip` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.country(o)` | `country` | `string` (ISO alpha-2) | 1 |
| `field.markdown(o)` | `markdown` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.code(o)` | `code` | `string` | 1 |
| `field.richText(o)` | `richText` | `string` (sanitized HTML) | 1 |
| `field.percent(o)` | `percent` | `number` (0 to 100) | 1 |
| `field.tags(o)` | `tags` | `string[]` | 1 (JSON) |
| `field.address(o)` | `address` | `Address` | 1 (JSON) |
| `field.dateRange(o)` | `dateRange` | `{ start: string; end: string }` | 1 (JSON) |
| `field.encrypted(o)` / `encryptedText(o)` / `encryptedJson(o)` | `encrypted` | `string` or `unknown` | 1, or 2 with `deterministic` |
| `field.fk(() => M, o)` | `fk` | `number \| string` (key `<name>Id`) | 1: `<name>Id` |
| `field.m2m(() => M, o)` | `m2m` | none on the row | 0 (through table) |

## Common options

Every builder takes an optional `Opts` object. Options a kind does not use are ignored unless noted.

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `optional` | `boolean` | `false` | Column is nullable; the value type becomes `V \| null`; may be left out on create (stored as NULL). |
| `default` | constant | none | Value used when create leaves the field out. Also written as the column `DEFAULT` (must be a literal: string, number, boolean, null, or what the field converts to one). |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | `UNIQUE` on the (first) column. Violations → `DomainError('domain', '<model>.<field> must be unique')`. |
| `index` | `boolean` | `false` | Creates index `<model>_<field>_idx` (in migrations). |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | Field joins the model's default `.search(term)` fields. Not allowed on money. |
| `hidden` | `boolean` | `false` (`true` for encrypted) | Left out of generic views' default serializer output. No DDL. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Generic views never accept it as create / update input. No DDL. |
| `writeOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Generic views accept it as input but never output it. No DDL. |
| `humanOnly` | `boolean \| string` | `false` | An agent-marked request that changes this field (admin save, generic views) is refused with `human_only`. A string is the reason shown. No DDL. |
| `auto` | `boolean` | `false` | datetime: set to now on create (same as `autoNowAdd`; legacy name). |
| `autoNowAdd` | `boolean` | `false` | date / datetime: set to now on create. |
| `autoNow` | `boolean` | `false` | date / datetime: set to now on create and on every `Model.update()`. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | per kind | email / url / slug / markdown / code / richText / tags (per tag). See each kind. Not enforced on `text`. |
| `maxDigits` | `number` | `12` | decimal: total digits. |
| `decimalPlaces` | `number` | `2` | decimal: digits after the point. |
| `uploadTo` | `string` | none | file / image: storage key prefix, e.g. `'avatars'`. |
| `onDelete` | `OnDelete` | `'RESTRICT'` | fk only. See [models.md](models.md#ondelete-fk-only). |
| `relatedName` | `string` | `<model>_set` | fk / m2m: reverse accessor name on the target. No DDL. |
| `language` | `string` | none | code: `'json' \| 'js' \| 'sql' \| 'html' \| 'css'`; `'json'` validates. |
| `maxItems` | `number` | `100` | tags: maximum number of tags. |
| `choices` | `string[]` | none | tags: only these values are allowed. |
| `allowRemoteImages` | `boolean` | `false` | richText: keep `http(s)` `<img>` sources. No DDL. |

Options marked "No DDL" never enter migrations; changing them needs no `makemigrations`.

## Field reference

Each table lists the JavaScript value, what input is accepted, the column type per database, and the admin widget (`contrib/admin/meta.ts kindOf`).

### field.id()

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `number` (integer), generated by the database |
| SQLite | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` |
| Postgres | `BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY` |
| MySQL | `BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY` |
| Admin | `int`, read-only |
| Options | none (takes no arguments) |

Must be named `id`. Every model needs `id: field.id()` or `id: field.uuid()`.

### field.uuid(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `string` |
| Accepts | any string (`z.string()`); filled with `crypto.randomUUID()` on create when left out |
| SQLite | `TEXT` |
| Postgres | `UUID` |
| MySQL | `CHAR(36)` |
| Admin | `uuid` |
| As pk | `id: field.uuid()` → `PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL` |

### field.text(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `string` |
| Accepts | any string; `maxLength` is NOT checked |
| SQLite | `TEXT` |
| Postgres | `TEXT` |
| MySQL | `LONGTEXT`; `VARCHAR(255)` when `unique` or `index` |
| Admin | `password` if named `password` (or `hidden` and name contains "password"); `email` if the name contains "email"; `url` if the name ends in `url` / `Url` / `URL`; `slug` if named `slug`; `textarea` if `maxLength > 255`; else `text` |

### field.int(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `number` (integer) |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `INTEGER` / `BIGINT` / `BIGINT` |
| Admin | `int` |

Supports `inc(n)` / `dec(n)` in `QuerySet.update()`.

### field.float(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `number` |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `REAL` / `DOUBLE PRECISION` / `DOUBLE` |
| Admin | `decimal` |

Supports `inc(n)` / `dec(n)`.

### field.bool(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `boolean` |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `INTEGER` (1/0) / `BOOLEAN` / `TINYINT(1)` |
| Admin | `bool` (never "required") |

### field.money(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `{ value: number; currency: string }`, `value` in major units (`29.99`) |
| Accepts | `value` with at most 2 decimals and absolute value below 1e12; `currency` any non-empty string |
| Columns | `<name>` = integer cents, `<name>Currency` |
| SQLite | `INTEGER`, `TEXT` |
| Postgres | `BIGINT`, `TEXT` |
| MySQL | `BIGINT`, `VARCHAR(3)` |
| Admin | `money` (2 decimals; currency from `default.currency`) |
| Not allowed | `searchable`; lookups `contains`, `startswith`, `endswith`, `iexact` |

Filters: `{ price: { value: 10, currency: 'USD' } }` compares amount and currency; a bare number (`price__gte: 10`) compares the amount in any currency. `price__currency: 'EUR'` filters the currency column. Ordering uses the amount. Every currency is treated as 2 minor digits.

### field.enum(values, opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | one of `values` (typed as the union) |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `TEXT` / `TEXT` / `VARCHAR(255)` |
| Admin | `choice`; labels from the value (`'in_stock'` → `'In stock'`) |

### field.datetime(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `Date` |
| Accepts | `Date` |
| SQLite | `INTEGER` (epoch milliseconds) |
| Postgres | `TIMESTAMPTZ` |
| MySQL | `DATETIME(3)` holding UTC; years 1000 to 9999 only |
| Admin | `datetime` |
| Options | `auto`, `autoNowAdd`, `autoNow` |

Lookups: `createdAt__year`, `__month`, `__day`, `__date` (UTC). See [queryset.md](queryset.md#lookups).

### field.date(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `string` `'YYYY-MM-DD'` |
| Accepts | that string (a real calendar day) or a `Date` (its UTC day) |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `TEXT` / `DATE` / `DATE` |
| Admin | `date` |
| Options | `autoNowAdd`, `autoNow` (today, UTC) |

### field.time(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `'HH:MM:SS'`, or `'HH:MM:SS.ffffff'` when microseconds are not zero |
| Accepts | `'HH:MM'`, `'HH:MM:SS'`, `'HH:MM:SS.f'` up to 6 digits |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `TEXT` / `TIME` / `TIME(6)` |
| Admin | `time` |

### field.duration(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `number` of milliseconds (fractions keep microseconds) |
| Stored | integer microseconds |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `INTEGER` / `BIGINT` / `BIGINT` |
| Admin | `duration` (the form shows seconds) |

### field.decimal(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `string` with exactly `decimalPlaces` decimals (`'12.50'`) |
| Accepts | a decimal string or a number; refused when over `maxDigits` / `decimalPlaces` |
| SQLite | `NUMERIC` (exact up to about 15 digits) |
| Postgres | `NUMERIC(maxDigits, decimalPlaces)` |
| MySQL | `DECIMAL(maxDigits, decimalPlaces)` |
| Admin | `decimal` |
| Options | `maxDigits` (12), `decimalPlaces` (2) |

### field.email(opts) / field.url(opts) / field.slug(opts)

| | email | url | slug |
|---|---|---|---|
| Value | `string` | `string` | `string` |
| Accepts | valid email | URL with scheme `http`, `https`, `ftp` or `ftps` | letters, digits, `_`, `-` |
| `maxLength` default | 254 | 200 | 50 |
| SQLite | `TEXT` | `TEXT` | `TEXT` |
| Postgres / MySQL | `VARCHAR(maxLength)` | `VARCHAR(maxLength)` | `VARCHAR(maxLength)` |
| Admin | `email` | `url` | `slug` |

### field.file(opts) / field.image(opts) / field.signature(opts)

| | file | image | signature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Value | storage key `string` (max 512) | same | same |
| Kind | `file` | `image` | `image` |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `TEXT` / `TEXT` / `VARCHAR(512)` | same | same |
| Admin | `file` (accept `application/pdf,image/*`) | `image` (accept `image/*`) | `signature` (drawn by hand) |
| Options | `uploadTo` | `uploadTo` | defaults `humanOnly: 'a signature must be drawn by a person'` |

The column holds the key that `defineUpload({ uploadTo })` returned; the file lives in `settings.media` storage. See [contrib/media.md](contrib/media.md). Any `image` field with `humanOnly` shows as the signature widget.

### field.json(opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | any JSON value (`unknown`) |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `TEXT` / `JSONB` / `JSON` |
| Admin | `json` |

### Input-shaped fields

Each is plain text, a number or JSON in the database, with its own validation, and maps to its own admin widget.

| Builder | Value / validation | SQLite | Postgres | MySQL | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | `#rrggbb`, stored lowercase | `TEXT` | `VARCHAR(7)` | `VARCHAR(7)` | `color` |
| `phone` | E.164, e.g. `+15551234567` | `TEXT` | `VARCHAR(16)` | `VARCHAR(16)` | `phone` |
| `ip` | IPv4 or IPv6, stored lowercase | `TEXT` | `VARCHAR(45)` | `VARCHAR(45)` | `ip` |
| `country` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. `'IS'` | `TEXT` | `VARCHAR(2)` | `VARCHAR(2)` | `country` |
| `markdown` | string, at most `maxLength` (default 100 000) | `TEXT` | `TEXT` | `LONGTEXT` | `markdown` |
| `code` | string, at most `maxLength` (default 100 000); `language: 'json'` must parse (empty allowed) | `TEXT` | `TEXT` | `LONGTEXT` | `code` |
| `richText` | HTML, sanitized to an allowlist on every save; `maxLength` counts visible text | `TEXT` | `TEXT` | `LONGTEXT` | `rich` |
| `percent` | number 0 to 100 | `REAL` | `DOUBLE PRECISION` | `DOUBLE` | `percent` |
| `tags` | `string[]`: each trimmed, 1 to `maxLength` (50) chars, deduped, at most `maxItems` (100), only `choices` if given | `TEXT` | `JSONB` | `JSON` | `tags` |
| `address` | `{ line1, line2?, city, region?, postal?, country }`; parts up to 200 chars, `postal` up to 20, `country` ISO; no extra keys | `TEXT` | `JSONB` | `JSON` | `address` |
| `dateRange` | `{ start, end }` as `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, `start <= end`, inclusive | `TEXT` | `JSONB` | `JSON` | `daterange` |

### field.encrypted(opts)

Encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (keys from `settings.encryption`).

| | |
|---|---|
| Value | `string` (`of: 'text'`, default) or any JSON (`of: 'json'`) |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | `TEXT` / `TEXT` / `LONGTEXT` |
| Extra column | with `deterministic: true`: `<name>Hash` (`TEXT` / `TEXT` / `VARCHAR(64)`), an HMAC of the value |
| Admin | `text` or `json`, only shown with `hidden: false` |
| Default | `hidden: true` |
| Not allowed | `unique`, `index`, `searchable`, `default` (throws) |
| Filters | only `eq`, `ne`, `in` (and `isnull`), and only with `deterministic: true` |

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `of` | `'text' \| 'json'` | `'text'` | Value type. |
| `deterministic` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds the hash column so exact-match filters work. |
| `context` | `string` | none | Extra key-derivation context. |
| `bindAs` | `string` | `'<model>.<field>'` | The name each ciphertext is bound to; set it to the old name after a rename so old values still decrypt. |
| `bindRow` | `boolean` | `false` | Also bind to the row's pk (a ciphertext copied to another row fails). Needs a `uuid` pk; writes must name one row (`create`, `Model.update`, `bulkUpdate`, `filter({ id }).update`). |

`field.encryptedText(o)` = `encrypted({ ...o, of: 'text' })`; `field.encryptedJson(o)` = `encrypted({ ...o, of: 'json' })`. Key rotation: `tvine encryption rotate`. More: [contrib/security.md](contrib/security.md).

### field.fk(() => Target, opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Row key | `<name>Id` (`customer` → `customerId`) |
| Value | the target's pk: `number` (target pk `id`) or `string` (target pk `uuid`) |
| SQLite / Postgres / MySQL | int pk target: `INTEGER` / `BIGINT` / `BIGINT`; uuid pk target: `TEXT` / `UUID` / `CHAR(36)` |
| Constraint | `REFERENCES <target>(id) ON DELETE <action>` (MySQL: a named table constraint) |
| Admin | `fk` (select; `autocomplete` / `rawId` set in the ModelAdmin) |
| Options | `onDelete`, `relatedName`, plus common ones (`optional`, `unique` for one-to-one, `index`, `default`) |

### field.m2m(() => Target, opts)

| | |
|---|---|
| Row key | none (no column) |
| Storage | auto through table `<model>_<field>`, or `through` model |
| Admin | `m2m` (multiple select) |

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `through` | `() => ModelDef` | auto table | Custom through model with one fk to each side. |
| `relatedName` | `string` | `<model>_set` | Reverse accessor on the target. |

Only these two options are typed for m2m.

## Examples

A product catalog with most kinds:

```ts
import { defineModel, field } from 'tvine'

export const Supplier = defineModel('supplier', {
  id: field.uuid(),
  name: field.text({ unique: true }),
  website: field.url({ optional: true }),
  phone: field.phone({ optional: true }),
  country: field.country(),
  address: field.address({ optional: true }),
  apiKey: field.encryptedText({ optional: true }),
})

export const Item = defineModel('item', {
  id: field.id(),
  supplier: field.fk(() => Supplier, { onDelete: 'CASCADE', relatedName: 'items' }),
  slug: field.slug({ unique: true }),
  title: field.text({ searchable: true }),
  description: field.richText({ optional: true }),
  price: field.money(),
  weightKg: field.decimal({ maxDigits: 6, decimalPlaces: 3, optional: true }),
  discount: field.percent({ default: 0 }),
  colour: field.color({ optional: true }),
  labels: field.tags({ maxItems: 10, optional: true }),
  status: field.enum(['draft', 'live', 'retired'], { default: 'draft', index: true }),
  photo: field.image({ uploadTo: 'items', optional: true }),
  specs: field.json({ optional: true }),
  availableOn: field.date({ optional: true }),
  createdAt: field.datetime({ autoNowAdd: true }),
  updatedAt: field.datetime({ autoNow: true }),
})
```

Writing values of each shape:

```ts
const s = await Supplier.create({ name: 'Nordic Lamps', country: 'IS', apiKey: 'sk_live_123' })
await Item.create({
  supplierId: s.id,
  slug: 'desk-lamp',
  title: 'Desk lamp',
  price: { value: 29.99, currency: 'USD' },
  weightKg: '1.250',
  labels: ['desk', 'led', 'desk'],      // stored as ['desk', 'led']
  availableOn: '2026-12-01',
  specs: { watts: 9, dimmable: true },
})
```

Exact-match filter on an encrypted field:

```ts
export const Account = defineModel('account', {
  id: field.id(),
  taxId: field.encryptedText({ deterministic: true }),
})
const hit = await Account.objects.filter({ taxId: 'IS-1234' }).first()
```

## Gotchas

- `field.text({ maxLength })` does not validate length (only the admin uses it to pick a textarea). Use `email` / `url` / `slug` / `markdown`, or validate in the action's zod schema.
- On MySQL a plain `text` is `LONGTEXT`; adding `unique` or `index` makes it `VARCHAR(255)`, and longer values are refused.
- Any `uuid` field left out of `create()` gets a random UUID, not only the pk, even when `optional`.
- `decimal` values come back as strings, `money` as `{ value, currency }`, `date` / `time` as strings, `datetime` as `Date`.
- `contains`, `startswith`, `endswith` are case-insensitive on every engine (they all lower both sides).
- Changing a field so its column set changes (int to fk, money to a scalar) cannot be auto-migrated; see [migrations.md](migrations.md).
- `default` is a constant, not a function.

Not covered by the code: per-field `validators`, `choices` on text (use `field.enum`), `verboseName` / `helpText` (the admin derives labels from names), `blank` separate from `null` (`optional` is both), `editable`, `db_column`, generated columns.

## See also

- [models.md](models.md) — `defineModel`, Meta, relations
- [queryset.md](queryset.md) — lookups each field supports
- [migrations.md](migrations.md) — what a field change does to the table
- [database.md](database.md) — engines and their types
- [contrib/admin.md](contrib/admin.md) — widgets, `formfieldOverrides`, `widgets`
- [contrib/media.md](contrib/media.md) — uploads for `file` / `image`
- [contrib/security.md](contrib/security.md) — encryption keys and rotation


# docs/reference/warp/queryset.md

# QuerySet

`Model.objects` is a `QuerySet`: a lazy, immutable description of a query. Chain methods (`filter`, `exclude`, `order`, `annotate`, ...) return a new QuerySet and run nothing. Terminal methods (`all`, `first`, `count`, `update`, ...) return a Promise and run SQL. Values always travel as bound parameters, never as SQL text. Source: `warp/src/data/queryset.ts`, `expressions.ts`, `sql/compile.ts`, `related.ts`, `paginator.ts`, `pending.ts`, `engine.ts`.

## Import

```ts
import {
  F, Q, Value, Case, When, Coalesce, Lower, Upper, Length, Abs, Cast, TruncDay, TruncMonth, TruncYear,
  Sum, Count, Avg, Min, Max, Exists, OuterRef, Subquery, Prefetch,
  Paginator, atomic, onCommit, defer, setOnCommitErrorHandler, inc, dec, type Page, type Paginated,
} from 'tvine'
```

Examples below use the shop models from [models.md](models.md#examples): `Customer`, `Product`, `Tag`, `Order` (fk `customer`, relatedName `orders`), `OrderItem` (fk `order` relatedName `items`, fk `product`).

## Chain methods (return a new QuerySet)

| Method | Signature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `filter` | `filter(where: Record<string, unknown> \| QNode \| Expression \| Where[])` | Keep rows matching every lookup (AND). Chained calls AND together. |
| `exclude` | `exclude(where)` | Drop rows matching ONE condition. A plain object with more than one key throws; chain calls or pass `Q(...)`. Null-inclusive: rows where the field is NULL are kept. |
| `order` | `order(...fields: (string \| OrderBy)[])` | Replace the order. `'name'` asc, `'-name'` desc, `'customer__name'` across a relation, an annotation name, or `F('x').desc({ nulls: 'last' })`. |
| `search` | `search(term: string, fields?: string[])` | Case-insensitive substring match OR-ed over `fields` (default: the model's `searchable` fields; throws if none). |
| `slice` | `slice(start: number, end?: number)` | `LIMIT` / `OFFSET`. Non-negative integers. A slice of a slice narrows it. |
| `limit` | `limit(n)` | `slice(0, n)` |
| `offset` | `offset(n)` | `slice(n)` |
| `annotate` | `annotate({ name: Expression, ... })` | Add computed columns. Names must be identifiers without `__` and must not clash with field names. An aggregate makes the query grouped. |
| `having` | `having(q: QNode \| Record<string, unknown>)` | Add a condition (a condition on an aggregate goes to `HAVING`; `filter` does that too). |
| `values` | `values(...names: string[])` | Return plain objects with only these keys (fields, annotations, relation paths). No names = every field + annotation. |
| `valuesList` | `valuesList(...names, { flat?: boolean })` | Return arrays (`[[1, 'Ada'], ...]`), or with `{ flat: true }` and exactly one name, the bare values (`[1, 2]`). |
| `distinct` | `distinct(...fields: string[])` | `SELECT DISTINCT`; with fields, `DISTINCT ON` (Postgres only; `order()` must start with the same fields). |
| `selectRelated` | `selectRelated(...paths: string[])` | Join fk chains (`'customer'`, `'order__customer'`) and attach each related row as an object under the fk name. Forward fk only. |
| `prefetchRelated` | `prefetchRelated(...lookups: (string \| PrefetchNode)[])` | After the main query, load relations with one extra query per hop (IN batched by 1000). Works for fk, reverse fk and m2m; `'items__product'` chains. |
| `selectForUpdate` | `selectForUpdate({ nowait?, skipLocked?, of? })` | `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`. Must run inside `atomic()`. `nowait` and `skipLocked` are exclusive. No-op on SQLite. |

Once a slice is taken, `filter`, `exclude`, `order`, `update`, `delete`, `aggregate` and `last` throw ("cannot ... a queryset once a slice has been taken").

## Terminal methods (return a Promise)

| Method | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `all(limit = Infinity)` | `T[]` | Every row (or the first `limit`). Fetches in cursor pages of 100, so large tables take several queries. |
| `fetchAll()` | `T[]` | Every row in ONE query. |
| `first()` | `T \| undefined` | First row under the current order. |
| `last()` | `T \| undefined` | Last row (order reversed, pk tie-break included). |
| `count()` | `number` | `COUNT(*)` of the filter (respects a slice). |
| `exists()` | `boolean` | Whether any row matches. |
| `page({ cursor?, size? }, count = true)` | `Paginated<T>` | One cursor page: `{ items, total?, pageSize, nextCursor? }`. `size` default 25, clamped to 1..100. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. Not for `values()` or sliced querysets. |
| `aggregate({ name: Aggregate })` | `{ [name]: value }` | One row of aggregates over the filter. |
| `inBulk(ids, { field? })` | `Record<string, T>` | Rows keyed by id (or by `field`), IN batched by 1000. |
| `update(patch)` | `number` | `UPDATE` matching rows; returns rows changed. Values validated per field; also takes `inc(n)`, `dec(n)` and expressions. Does NOT touch `autoNow` fields. |
| `delete()` | `number` | `DELETE` matching rows (no filter = every row); `onDelete` rules apply. |
| `getOrCreate(lookup, defaults = {})` | `[T, boolean]` | Find by `lookup` or create from its plain keys + `defaults`; `true` = created. Race-safe (insert-or-nothing, then re-read), in `atomic()`. |
| `updateOrCreate(lookup, defaults = {})` | `[T, boolean]` | Lock the match and write `defaults` to it, or create. |
| `bulkCreate(rows, { batchSize? })` | `T[]` | Multi-row INSERTs in one `atomic()` (at most 1000 rows / 30 000 params per statement). Give the id for every row or none. On MySQL the returned rows are the given rows (no auto ids). |
| `bulkUpdate(rows, fields, { batchSize? })` | `number` | Write `fields` of each row (each needs its pk) with one `CASE` UPDATE per batch, in one `atomic()`. |

## Lookups

A filter key is `path` or `path__lookup`. `path` is a field name (an fk may be written `customer` or `customerId`), an annotation name, or a relation path `a__b__c`.

| Lookup | Example | SQL meaning |
|---|---|---|
| (none) / `exact` / `eq` | `{ status: 'paid' }` | `=`; `null` value → `IS NULL` |
| `ne` | `{ status__ne: 'cart' }` | `<>`, NULL rows included (`IS NULL OR <> x`) |
| `gt` `gte` `lt` `lte` | `{ stock__lte: 5 }` | `>` `>=` `<` `<=` |
| `in` | `{ id__in: [1, 2, 3] }` | `IN (...)`; at most 1000 values; `[]` matches nothing; or a `Subquery(...)` |
| `range` | `{ createdAt__range: [from, to] }` | inclusive `BETWEEN`; exactly two non-null values |
| `contains` / `icontains` | `{ name__contains: 'lamp' }` | case-insensitive substring (both the same) |
| `startswith` / `istartswith` | `{ sku__startswith: 'LAMP' }` | case-insensitive prefix |
| `endswith` / `iendswith` | `{ email__endswith: '@example.com' }` | case-insensitive suffix |
| `iexact` | `{ email__iexact: 'Ada@Example.com' }` | case-insensitive equality; string only |
| `isnull` | `{ customer__isnull: true }` | `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` |
| `year` `month` `day` | `{ createdAt__year: 2026 }`, `{ createdAt__month__gte: 6 }` | date part (UTC) of a `date` / `datetime`; can be followed by a lookup |
| `date` | `{ createdAt__date: '2026-11-03' }` | the UTC day of a datetime as `'YYYY-MM-DD'` |
| `currency` | `{ total__currency: 'EUR' }` | the currency column of a money field |

`contains` is substring search on the column's text form, so it also works on numbers and uuids. Money refuses `contains`, `startswith`, `endswith`, `iexact`. Encrypted fields allow only exact match (see [fields.md](fields.md#fieldencryptedopts)).

### Relation spanning

| Path | Relation | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `customer__email` | forward fk | `Order.objects.filter({ customer__email: 'ada@example.com' })` |
| `orders__status` | reverse fk (by `relatedName`; default `<model>_set`) | `Customer.objects.filter({ orders__status: 'paid' })` |
| `tags__name` | m2m (either direction) | `Product.objects.filter({ tags__name: 'desk' })` |
| `items__product__sku` | several hops | `Order.objects.filter({ items__product__sku: 'LAMP-1' })` |
| `orders__isnull: true` | "has no related row" | customers with no orders |
| `orders` (bare) | the related pk | `Customer.objects.filter({ orders__in: [1, 2] })` |

Filters across relations compile to `IN (SELECT ...)` subqueries, so a row is never duplicated by a to-many relation. Inside ONE `filter()` call (or one `Q` AND node), several lookups through the same to-many relation must all hold for the SAME related row; separate `filter()` calls are independent.

### Values compared to fields and expressions

A lookup value may be an expression: `{ stock__lt: F('reorderAt') }`, `{ id__in: Subquery(qs.values('customer')) }`, `{ customer: OuterRef('id') }` inside a subquery.

## Q objects

```ts
Q(lookups?: Record<string, unknown> | Expression): QNode
q.and(...others: (QNode | Record<string, unknown> | Expression)[]): QNode
q.or(...others): QNode
q.not(): QNode
```

TypeScript has no `&` `|` `~` overloading: use `.and`, `.or`, `.not`. `exclude(Q(...))` negates the whole Q. Negation is null-inclusive.

## Expressions (`data/expressions.ts`)

| Builder | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `F(name)` | A field, annotation or relation path (`F('customer__name')`). |
| `Value(v)` | A literal parameter. Money: `Value({ value: 5, currency: 'USD' })`. |
| `expr.add(x)` `.sub(x)` `.mul(x)` `.div(x)` | Arithmetic; numeric fields only. Money: `+`/`-` another amount of the same currency; `*`/`/` a plain number (money on the left). |
| `expr.asc({ nulls? })` `expr.desc({ nulls? })` | An order term; `nulls: 'first' \| 'last'`. In `order()` only on `F(name)`; annotate other expressions first. |
| `Coalesce(...xs)` | First non-null. |
| `Lower(x)` `Upper(x)` | Unicode-aware case. |
| `Length(x)` | Character length (int). |
| `Abs(x)` | Absolute value. |
| `Cast(x, 'int' \| 'float' \| 'text')` | Type cast. |
| `TruncDay(x)` `TruncMonth(x)` `TruncYear(x)` | Datetime truncated in UTC; datetime fields only. |
| `Case(When(cond, then), ..., { default })` | Conditional value; at least one `When`. `cond` is lookups, a `Q` or a boolean expression. |
| `Subquery(qs)` | Scalar subquery (first row; use `.values('one')` to pick the column, else the pk), or the right side of `__in`. |
| `Exists(qs)` | Boolean; use in `filter()` or `annotate()`. |
| `OuterRef(name)` | A column of the outer query, inside `Subquery` / `Exists`. |
| `Prefetch(path, queryset?)` | A `prefetchRelated` hop with a custom queryset (filter / order the related rows). |

Strings passed where an expression is expected (`Lower('name')`, `Sum('total')`) are field references.

## Aggregates

```ts
Sum(x, { distinct?, filter? })   Avg(x, opts)   Min(x, opts)   Max(x, opts)
Count(x = '*', { distinct?, filter? })
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `distinct` | Aggregate distinct values only. |
| `filter` | Lookups or `Q`: only matching rows count. |

Results: `Count` is `0` on no rows; `Sum` / `Avg` / `Min` / `Max` are `null`. `Avg` is a float (on money: rounded to whole cents). `Sum` / `Avg` need a numeric field. On money they return `{ value, currency }`; if the rows mix currencies, reading the result throws `invalid_param` ("mixes currencies"): filter on `<field>__currency` or group by it. Aggregates cannot be nested. `aggregate()` is not supported over `values()`, `distinct()` or aggregate annotations.

Grouping (`values(...)` then `annotate(...)`): `values(...)` names become `GROUP BY` columns when an annotation is an aggregate. Without `values()`, an aggregate annotation groups per row of the model.

## Pagination

Cursor pages (`qs.page(...)`) are the default for lists. For "page 3 of 12" use `Paginator` (OFFSET / LIMIT):

```ts
new Paginator<T>(objectList: QuerySet<T>, perPage: number, opts?: { orphans?: number; allowEmptyFirstPage?: boolean })
```

| Member | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `count()` | `Promise<number>` | Total rows (one COUNT, cached). |
| `numPages()` | `Promise<number>` | At least 1, unless `allowEmptyFirstPage: false` and there are no rows. |
| `validateNumber(n)` | `Promise<number>` | Accepts an integer or a digit string; else `DomainError('invalid_param', ..., 'page')`. |
| `page(n)` | `Promise<Page<T>>` | `{ items, number, numPages, count, hasNext, hasPrevious, startIndex, endIndex }` (indexes 1-based, 0 when empty). |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `orphans` | `0` | If the last page would have this many items or fewer, they join the previous page. |
| `allowEmptyFirstPage` | `true` | Page 1 is valid even with no rows. |

## Transactions

```ts
atomic<R>(body: () => Promise<R>, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal; lazy?: boolean }): Promise<R>
onCommit(fn: () => unknown): void | Promise<void>
defer(fn: () => unknown): void
setOnCommitErrorHandler(fn: (e: unknown) => void): void
```

| Function | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `atomic(body)` | Runs `body` in one transaction: commit when it resolves, rollback when it throws (or `signal` aborts). A nested `atomic()` joins the outer block (no savepoints). Queries from the callback after the block ended throw. |
| `atomic(body, { lazy: true })` | The transaction opens at the first query; a block that never queries opens nothing. Used per request. |
| `onCommit(fn)` | Inside `atomic()`: run after the outermost commit, dropped on rollback. Outside: run now. From a block already rolled back: throws. A hook that throws after commit goes to the `setOnCommitErrorHandler` handler (default `console.error`), the commit stands. |
| `defer(fn)` | Like `onCommit`, but runs on the next tick outside any transaction and does not hold up the response; errors go to the `tvine.defer` logger. |

Every action that is not `readOnly` already runs inside a lazy `atomic()` when `settings.db.atomicRequests` is `true` (the default). See [database.md](database.md#settingsdb).

## Await or not

QuerySets are not thenables: `await Product.objects.filter(...)` gives back the QuerySet, not rows. Call a terminal method.

Every public ORM call is tracked by the enclosing scope (a request handler, an `atomic()` block, a task job):

- Calls run one after another in call order on the scope's connection.
- The scope waits for all of them before it ends (before COMMIT / before the reply), even ones you did not `await`.
- A failed call nobody awaited fails the scope like a throw (the request rolls back).

Tracked calls: reads `page`, `all`, `fetchAll`, `first`, `last`, `count`, `exists`, `aggregate`, `inBulk`, `Model.get`; writes `update`, `delete`, `getOrCreate`, `updateOrCreate`, `bulkCreate`, `bulkUpdate`, `Model.create`, `Model.update`, `Model.delete`, and `related(...).add / remove / set / clear`. Outside any scope (a script, top level), an un-awaited write still runs; the first one logs a warning on `tvine.db` and a failure is logged, not thrown. Await reads you need the result of.

## Examples

Filters, Q and ordering:

```ts
const cheap = await Product.objects.filter({ active: true, price__lt: 20 }).order('-stock', 'name').all()

const lowOrHidden = await Product.objects
  .filter(Q({ stock__lte: 5 }).or({ active: false }))
  .exclude({ sku__startswith: 'TEST' })
  .fetchAll()

const paidThisYear = await Order.objects
  .filter({ status: 'paid', createdAt__year: 2026, customer__email__endswith: '@example.com' })
  .count()
```

Updates with `inc` / `dec` / `F`, and a safe stock check in a transaction:

```ts
import { atomic, dec, DomainError, F } from 'tvine'

await atomic(async () => {
  const p = await Product.objects.filter({ id: 7 }).selectForUpdate().first()
  if (!p || p.stock < 2) throw new DomainError('domain', 'not enough stock', 'stock')
  await Product.objects.filter({ id: 7 }).update({ stock: dec(2) })
})
await Product.objects.filter({ active: true }).update({ stock: F('stock').add(10) })
```

Aggregates, grouping and annotations:

```ts
const totals = await Order.objects.filter({ status: 'paid', total__currency: 'USD' })
  .aggregate({ revenue: Sum('total'), orders: Count(), avg: Avg('total') })
// { revenue: { value: 1234.5, currency: 'USD' }, orders: 42, avg: { value: 29.39, currency: 'USD' } }

const byStatus = await Order.objects.values('status').annotate({ n: Count() }).order('status').all()
// [{ status: 'cart', n: 3 }, { status: 'paid', n: 42 }]

const loyal = await Customer.objects
  .annotate({ orderCount: Count('orders') })     // LEFT JOIN order, GROUP BY customer
  .filter({ orderCount__gte: 3 })                // goes to HAVING
  .order('-orderCount')
  .all()

const paidPerCustomer = await Order.objects.filter({ status: 'paid' })
  .values('customer').annotate({ n: Count() }).order('customer').all()   // [{ customer: 1, n: 4 }, ...]

const labelled = await Order.objects.annotate({
  size: Case(When({ total__gte: 100 }, 'large'), { default: 'small' }),
  day: TruncDay('createdAt'),
}).values('id', 'size', 'day').all()
```

Subqueries and Exists:

```ts
const buyers = await Customer.objects
  .filter(Exists(Order.objects.filter({ customer: OuterRef('id'), status: 'paid' })))
  .all()

const withLast = await Customer.objects.annotate({
  lastOrderAt: Subquery(Order.objects.filter({ customer: OuterRef('id') }).order('-createdAt').values('createdAt')),
}).all()

const tagged = await Product.objects
  .filter({ id__in: Subquery(Product.objects.filter({ tags__name: 'desk' }).values('id')) })
  .valuesList('sku', { flat: true })
  .all()   // ['LAMP-1', ...]
```

Related rows, pages and get-or-create:

```ts
type OrderWith = Order & { customer: Customer; items: { productId: number; quantity: number }[] }
const recent = await Order.objects.selectRelated('customer').prefetchRelated('items').limit(20).all() as OrderWith[]
recent[0]?.customer.email

const page1 = await Product.objects.filter({ active: true }).page({ size: 50 })
const page2 = await Product.objects.filter({ active: true }).page({ size: 50, cursor: page1.nextCursor })

const [tag, created] = await Tag.objects.getOrCreate({ name: 'desk' })

const pager = new Paginator(Product.objects.filter({ active: true }), 20, { orphans: 3 })
const p3 = await pager.page(3)   // { items, number: 3, numPages, count, hasNext, ... }
```

## Gotchas

- `exclude({ a: 1, b: 2 })` throws. Chain `.exclude({ a: 1 }).exclude({ b: 2 })` (NOT a AND NOT b) or use `exclude(Q({ a: 1, b: 2 }))` (NOT (a AND b)).
- `exclude` and `ne` keep NULL rows (`exclude({ status: 'paid' })` returns rows with `status` NULL too).
- `contains`, `startswith`, `endswith` are always case-insensitive. There is no case-sensitive substring lookup.
- `__in` accepts at most 1000 values; split the list or use `Subquery`.
- `selectRelated` / `prefetchRelated` attach objects that the row type does not show; cast as in the example.
- `Meta.ordering` applies to every query without `.order()`, including `values().annotate()` groupings. Its column is then in ORDER BY but not in GROUP BY: SQLite accepts that, Postgres refuses it. Call `.order(...)` with grouped columns on grouped queries.
- `F()` in `update()` cannot cross relations; filters in `update()` / `delete()` can.
- `QuerySet.update()` skips `autoNow`; use `Model.update(id, patch)` when the timestamp must move.
- `all()` on a big table runs one query per 100 rows (cursor loop). Use `fetchAll()` for one query, or `page()` for real paging.
- `distinct('field')` is Postgres only.
- Inside an aggregate's `filter`, a relation path (`Count('orders', { filter: { orders__status: 'paid' } })`) is an IN subquery on the OUTER row, not a test of each joined row, so it does not count per related row. Aggregate from the related model instead (`Order.objects.filter({ status: 'paid' }).values('customer').annotate({ n: Count() })`). Plain fields of the aggregated model in `filter` work as expected.

Not covered by the code: a raw SQL query API (`raw()`, `extra()`, a cursor), `iterator()`, `union` / `intersection` / `difference`, `only` / `defer` column lists, `reverse()`, `dates()`, `get()` on a QuerySet (use `first()` or `Model.get(id)`), savepoints inside nested `atomic()`. The only raw SQL is `ops.runSQL` in migrations.

## See also

- [models.md](models.md) — the models used above, `related()` managers
- [fields.md](fields.md) — per-field values and filter support
- [database.md](database.md) — engines, pooling, `atomicRequests`
- [views.md](views.md) — generic views that build querysets from requests
- [errors.md](errors.md) — `DomainError` codes


# docs/reference/warp/migrations.md

# Migrations and fixtures

Each app has code files `apps/<app>/migrations/NNNN_name.ts`, each exporting `migration({ dependencies, operations })`. There is no state file: the schema state is rebuilt by replaying every migration in dependency order, and `makemigrations` diffs that state against the current `models.ts`. `migrate` renders each operation for the connected database at apply time and records it in the table `__tvine_migrations (app, name, checksum, applied_at)`. Fixtures (`dumpdata` / `loaddata`) move rows in and out as JSON. Source: `warp/src/data/migrations.ts`, `migrate.ts`, `schema/*.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, `cli.ts`.

## Import

```ts
import { migration, ops, field } from 'tvine/migrations'          // inside migration files
import { makeMigrations, migrate, migrateCheck } from 'tvine'      // programmatic use
```

## CLI commands

| Command | Flags | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `tvine makemigrations` | `--name x`, `--allow-drop`, `--merge`, `--empty`, `--check`, `--dry-run` | Diff models against migrations, write new files per changed app. |
| `tvine makemigrations <app> --empty` | `--name x` | Write an empty migration for hand-written operations. (An app argument works only with `--empty`.) |
| `tvine migrate` | `--plan`, `--fake`, `--check` | Apply every unapplied migration, then run apps' `postMigrate` hooks. |
| `tvine migrate <app>` | same | Apply that app up to its latest migration (and what it depends on). |
| `tvine migrate <app> <target>` | same | Go forward OR roll back to `<target>` (a name or a unique prefix like `0002`). |
| `tvine migrate <app> zero` | same | Roll back every migration of the app (and everything depending on them). |
| `tvine sqlmigrate <app> <migration>` | `--backwards` | Print the SQL for the connected database's dialect, with params. |
| `tvine showmigrations` | | Every migration per app, `[X]` applied / `[ ]` not. |
| `tvine dumpdata [app[.model] ...]` | `--output f.json` | Rows as fixture JSON (stdout or file). |
| `tvine loaddata <f.json> ...` | | Load fixture files in ONE transaction, upsert by pk. |
| `tvine check` | | Includes "migrations pending" and "models.ts changed since the last migration". |

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--name x` | Use `NNNN_x` instead of the automatic name. Letters, digits, `_`. |
| `--allow-drop` | Confirm a migration that removes fields or models. Without it `makemigrations` refuses. |
| `--merge` | For an app with two leaf migrations (two branches), write a merge migration depending on both. |
| `--empty` | Empty migration for `<app>`. |
| `--check` (makemigrations) | Dry run; exit 1 if a migration would be written. |
| `--dry-run` | Report the files, write nothing. |
| `--plan` | List what would apply (or roll back); touch nothing. |
| `--fake` | Record as applied (or unapplied) without running SQL. |
| `--check` (migrate) | Exit 1 if migrations are pending, edited, conflicting, or models drifted. Takes no app / target. |

`--check`, `--plan` and `--fake` are mutually exclusive on `migrate`.

## Automatic names

`0001_initial` for an app's first migration. Later ones join one fragment per operation: `<model>` (createModel), `delete_<model>`, `<model>_<field>` (addField), `remove_<model>_<field>`, `alter_<model>_<field>`. Any other operation, or a name over 52 characters, gives `NNNN_auto`. Numbers are the app's highest + 1, zero-padded to 4.

## File format

```ts
// apps/shop/migrations/0002_product_stock.ts
import { migration, ops, field } from 'tvine/migrations'

export default migration({
  dependencies: [
    ['shop', '0001_initial'],
  ],
  operations: [
    ops.addField('product', 'stock', field.int({ default: 0 })),
  ],
})
```

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dependencies` | `[app, 'NNNN_name']` pairs. Its own app's previous migration, plus the latest migration of any app it points an fk at. |
| `operations` | Run in order. |
| `field` | Same builders as models, except `field.fk('customer', opts)` and `field.m2m('tag', { through?: 'product_tag', ... })` take the target model NAME (a migration never imports models). |

Files are found by the pattern `NNNN_name.(ts|mts|js|mjs)`; a `.ts` wins over a `.js` of the same name. A file that removes something starts with `// DESTRUCTIVE: drops ...`. Generated files are deterministic.

Checksum: `sha256` of the migration's data (dependencies + operations, key-sorted). Comments and formatting do not count. Editing the data of an applied migration makes `migrate` fail with `migration <app>.<name> was edited after it was applied`.

## Operations (`ops`)

| Operation | Signature | Reverse (rollback) |
|---|---|---|
| `createModel` | `ops.createModel(model, fields, meta?: { indexes?: Record<name, { fields, unique? }>; unique?: string[][]; constraints?: Record<name, ConstraintSpec> })` | deleteModel |
| `deleteModel` | `ops.deleteModel(model)` | recreate from the previous state |
| `addField` | `ops.addField(model, name, field)` | removeField |
| `removeField` | `ops.removeField(model, name)` | addField from the previous state; refused if the field was required without a default, or if removing it also dropped constraints |
| `alterField` | `ops.alterField(model, name, field)` | alterField back to the previous spec |
| `renameField` | `ops.renameField(model, from, to)` | rename back |
| `renameModel` | `ops.renameModel(from, to)` | rename back |
| `addIndex` | `ops.addIndex(model, name, fields, { unique? })` | removeIndex |
| `removeIndex` | `ops.removeIndex(model, name)` | addIndex |
| `addConstraint` | `ops.addConstraint(model, CheckConstraint(...) \| UniqueConstraint(...))` | removeConstraint |
| `removeConstraint` | `ops.removeConstraint(model, name)` | addConstraint |
| `alterUniqueTogether` | `ops.alterUniqueTogether(model, unique: string[][])` | the previous sets |
| `runSQL` | `ops.runSQL(sql, { reverse? })` | `reverse`; without it the migration cannot be rolled back |

`runSQL` arguments: `sql` is a string, an array of strings (one per statement), or a per-database object `{ sqlite?, postgres?, mysql? }` of those. `reverse` has the same shape; `[]` means "nothing to undo". A per-database object missing the connected database throws `runSQL has no SQL for <db>`.

What the autodetector writes:

- Removals first (Meta constraints / indexes / unique sets that changed, then removed fields, then deleted models), then new models (fk targets first), new fields, altered fields, and last the new Meta indexes / unique sets / constraints.
- Renames are never guessed: a renamed field is `removeField` + `addField` and needs `--allow-drop`. The error message prints the `ops.renameField(...)` / `ops.renameModel(...)` line to write by hand instead.
- Field options with no DDL (`hidden`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly`, `relatedName`, `humanOnly`, `allowRemoteImages`) never appear in migrations.

## What makemigrations refuses

| Situation | Message (short) | Do instead |
|---|---|---|
| A field or model would be dropped | `refusing to write a migration that drops ...` | `--allow-drop`, or write `ops.renameField` / `ops.renameModel` |
| New required field, no default | `field <m>.<f> is required and has no default` | add `default`, make it `optional`, or add in two steps (optional, backfill, then required) |
| Column set changes (int → fk, money ↔ scalar) | `column shape changed for <m>.<f>` | `removeField` + `addField` (`--allow-drop`) or `runSQL` |
| Two leaf migrations in one app | `conflicting migrations in <app>` | `makemigrations --merge` |
| Circular fk dependency across apps | `circular migration dependency` | split the fk into a later migration |

`alterField` is also refused at migrate time when it would round stored values (`<type> → <type>`), change an fk target, or change an m2m's kind / target / through. Renaming an auto m2m field, or a model that owns or is the target of an auto m2m, needs `runSQL`. A required `autoNow` / `autoNowAdd` field added to an existing table is added nullable, backfilled with the migration time, then made required.

## How migrate runs

| Database | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| SQLite | One transaction per migration (with its journal row). Foreign keys are turned off for the migration and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` runs before commit. SQLite cannot ALTER a column, so `alterField` / `removeField` rebuild the table (create new, copy, drop, rename, re-index). |
| Postgres | One transaction per migration; native `ALTER`. A transaction-level advisory lock serializes concurrent `migrate` runs; a migration another run already applied is skipped. |
| MySQL / MariaDB | DDL auto-commits, so each statement is applied and journaled on its own (`NNNN_name#op.stmt` rows). After a failure, fix the cause and run `migrate` again: it resumes. A session lock (`GET_LOCK`, 600 s) serializes concurrent runs. |

After a non-`--plan` run, the CLI calls every installed app's `hooks.ts` `postMigrate({ app, models, applied })` (tvine.auth creates permission rows there).

Rollback computes every reverse statement before running any, so an irreversible operation (runSQL without `reverse`, a lossy change) refuses with nothing touched.

## Built-in app migrations

Contrib apps (`tvine.auth`, `tvine.tasks`, `tvine.admin`, `tvine.audit`, `tvine.shield`) ship their own migrations under their label (`auth`, `tasks`, ...). They join the graph when the app is in `installedApps`, are never written by `makemigrations`, and `makemigrations --empty auth` is refused. With a custom `settings.auth.userModel`, tvine.auth's migrations are rewritten to point at your user table and depend on your user app's first migration.

## Programmatic API

```ts
makeMigrations(appsDir: string, opts?: { name?: string; allowDrop?: boolean; merge?: boolean; empty?: string; dryRun?: boolean; installed?: readonly string[] }): Promise<{ files: string[]; message: string }>
migrate(db: string | Connection, appsDir: string, opts?: { plan?: boolean; fake?: boolean; app?: string; target?: string; installed?: readonly string[] }): Promise<{ applied: string[]; unapplied?: string[] }>
migrateCheck(db: string | Connection, appsDir: string, opts?: { installed?: readonly string[] }): Promise<boolean>
```

`db` is a database URL (opened and closed for the call) or an open connection. `installed` is `settings.installedApps`; leave it out and contrib apps are not included. These do not run `postMigrate` hooks (the CLI does).

## Data migrations

There is no `RunPython` operation. Options the code offers:

- `ops.runSQL(...)` with per-database SQL and a `reverse`.
- An empty migration (`makemigrations <app> --empty`) holding `runSQL`.
- Changing data with the ORM from a script, an action, or a `postMigrate` hook in `apps/<app>/hooks.ts`.

## Fixtures

Format: a JSON array of rows.

```json
[
  { "model": "shop.customer", "pk": 1, "fields": { "email": "ada@example.com", "name": "Ada", "joinedAt": "2026-11-03T10:00:00.000Z" } },
  { "model": "shop.product", "pk": 7, "fields": { "sku": "LAMP-1", "name": "Desk lamp", "price": { "value": 29.99, "currency": "USD" }, "stock": 4, "active": true, "tags": [1, 2], "updatedAt": "2026-11-03T10:00:00.000Z" } },
  { "model": "shop.order", "pk": 1, "fields": { "customerId": 1, "status": "paid", "total": { "value": 59.98, "currency": "USD" }, "createdAt": "2026-11-03T10:05:00.000Z" } }
]
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `model` | `'<app>.<model name>'` (app label = folder name; model name as given to `defineModel`). |
| `pk` | The primary key value. |
| `fields` | Every other column by row key (`customerId` for an fk); datetimes as ISO strings; m2m (auto through only) as a list of target pks. |

`dumpdata` writes models in fk order (targets first), rows ordered by pk. `loaddata`:

- loads every given file in ONE `atomic()` block;
- creates a row if its pk is new, otherwise updates it (through `Model.create` / `Model.update`, so fields validate and convert as usual);
- orders rows so fk targets load first; required self-fks load parents first (a cycle is refused); optional self-fks are set after all rows exist;
- sets m2m lists with `related(name, pk).set(ids)`;
- resets Postgres id sequences afterwards.

Not covered: `dumpData` / `loadData` are not exported from `tvine`; use the CLI.

## Examples

Hand-written rename plus data fix:

```ts
// apps/shop/migrations/0003_rename_title.ts
import { migration, ops } from 'tvine/migrations'

export default migration({
  dependencies: [['shop', '0002_product_stock']],
  operations: [
    ops.renameField('product', 'title', 'name'),
    ops.runSQL(`UPDATE "product" SET "stock" = 0 WHERE "stock" < 0`, { reverse: [] }),
  ],
})
```

Per-database SQL:

```ts
ops.runSQL(
  { postgres: 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm', sqlite: [], mysql: [] },
  { reverse: [] },
)
```

A model with an fk to another app, Meta index and constraint (what `makemigrations` writes):

```ts
import { migration, ops, field } from 'tvine/migrations'

export default migration({
  dependencies: [['shop', '0001_initial'], ['crm', '0001_initial']],
  operations: [
    ops.createModel('review', {
      id: field.id(),
      product: field.fk('product', { onDelete: 'CASCADE' }),
      customer: field.fk('customer', { onDelete: 'CASCADE' }),
      stars: field.int(),
    }, {
      indexes: { review_product_stars_idx: { fields: ['product', 'stars'] } },
      constraints: { review_stars_range: { kind: 'check', name: 'review_stars_range', check: { conn: 'and', items: [['stars__gte', 1], ['stars__lte', 5]] } } },
    }),
  ],
})
```

Typical workflow:

```bash
tvine makemigrations            # created shop/migrations/0002_product_stock.ts
tvine migrate --plan            # planned: shop.0002_product_stock
tvine migrate                   # applied shop.0002_product_stock
tvine migrate shop 0001         # roll back to 0001
tvine dumpdata shop --output shop.json
tvine loaddata shop.json        # installed 12 object(s) from 1 fixture(s)
```

## Gotchas

- Never edit an applied migration's operations; write a new one. Comments and formatting are safe.
- A rename needs a hand-written `ops.renameField` / `ops.renameModel`; letting `--allow-drop` through loses the column's data.
- `runSQL` without `reverse` makes the migration (and `migrate <app> <earlier>`) impossible to roll back.
- On MySQL a failed migration stays half-applied; `migrate` again resumes it. To change the migration instead, undo by hand and delete its `NNNN_name#...` rows from `__tvine_migrations`.
- Choose `settings.auth.userModel` before the first `migrate`.
- `migrate` does not run on server start; deploy scripts run `tvine migrate && tvine start` (the scaffolded `start` script).
- `makemigrations` writes constraints as plain data (`{ kind: 'check', name, check: { conn, items } }`). `CheckConstraint(...)` / `UniqueConstraint(...)` from `tvine` return that same data, so a hand-written file may use either.
- `ops.deleteModel` can be rolled back, but only the empty table comes back; its rows are gone.

Not covered by the code: `squashmigrations`, `RunPython`, `SeparateDatabaseAndState`, per-migration `atomic = False`, migrating several database aliases.

## See also

- [models.md](models.md) — Meta indexes, unique sets, constraints
- [fields.md](fields.md) — which options reach the DDL
- [database.md](database.md) — engines, `DATABASE_URL`, test databases
- [contrib/auth.md](contrib/auth.md) — custom user model and its migrations
- [overview.md](overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/database.md

# Database

Warp talks to SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL / MariaDB through one small driver interface. Which one is used depends only on the database URL. Models never hold a connection: each query looks up the connection when it runs, so defining or importing models opens nothing, and the Postgres / MySQL pool connects on its first query. Source: `warp/src/data/db.ts`, `driver.ts`, `engine.ts`, `sql/dialect.ts`, `sql/dialects/*.ts`, `adapters/memory.ts`, `settings.ts`.

## Import

```ts
import { configureDb, closeDb, atomic, defineSettings } from 'tvine'
```

## Engines

| Engine | URL | Driver package | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SQLite | `file:./tvine.db`, `file:/abs/path.db`, a bare path ending in `.db` / `.sqlite` / `.sqlite3`, `:memory:`, `file::memory:` | `better-sqlite3` (a dependency) | One connection per process. Opened with `journal_mode = WAL`, `busy_timeout = 5000`, `foreign_keys = ON`. All operations go through one serial queue; `atomic()` uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. |
| PostgreSQL | `postgres://...` or `postgresql://...` | `pg` (optional peer dependency: `npm i pg`) | `pg.Pool`, one connection per statement; `atomic()` holds one connection for the block. `int8` values come back as JS numbers (an unsafe integer throws). |
| MySQL / MariaDB | `mysql://...` or `mariadb://...` | `mysql2` (optional peer dependency: `npm i mysql2`) | Pool; every new connection gets strict `sql_mode`, `time_zone = '+00:00'`, `READ COMMITTED`, charset `utf8mb4_bin`. Server-side prepared statements. |

Any other URL is refused (`unsupported database url ...`); error messages never echo the user / password.

MySQL URL query parameters (anything else is refused):

| Param | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ssl` | `true`, `1`, `false`, `0` | TLS with certificate check, or none. |
| `sslmode` | `disable`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full` | `require` = encrypt without verifying the certificate; `verify-*` = verify. |

Postgres URLs are passed to `pg` as `connectionString`, so `pg`'s own URL options apply.

### Differences that show up in your code

| Topic | SQLite | Postgres | MySQL |
|---|---|---|---|
| DDL in a transaction | yes | yes | no (migrations resume step by step) |
| `INSERT ... RETURNING` | yes | yes | no: the row is read back by pk; `bulkCreate` returns the given rows without auto ids |
| `selectForUpdate()` | no-op (the write lock is already held) | `FOR UPDATE [OF] [NOWAIT \| SKIP LOCKED]` | same as Postgres |
| `distinct('field')` | refused | `DISTINCT ON` | refused |
| Unicode case-insensitive lookups | yes (custom `tv_lower`) | yes | yes |
| `datetime` storage | epoch ms integer | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | `DATETIME(3)` UTC, years 1000 to 9999 |
| `text` with `unique` / `index` | `TEXT` | `TEXT` | `VARCHAR(255)` |
| `onDelete: 'SET_DEFAULT'` | database | database | done by the ORM before the delete |
| Statement parameter limit used | 30 000 per statement (bulk writes are batched) | same | same |

Per-field column types: [fields.md](fields.md).

## settings.db

```ts
db: {
  url: string                     // default: DATABASE_URL, else 'file:./tvine.db'
  pool: { max: number; acquireMs: number; idleMs: number }
  atomicRequests: boolean
  slowQueryMs: number
}
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | `DATABASE_URL` env, else `'file:./tvine.db'` | Which database. An explicit setting wins over the env var. `DATABASE_URL` set but blank throws (it never silently falls back to SQLite). An empty `url` fails settings validation. |
| `pool.max` | `number` | `10` | Postgres / MySQL pool size. |
| `pool.acquireMs` | `number` | `5000` | Max wait for a free connection; then `DomainError('internal', 'db busy — retry')`. |
| `pool.idleMs` | `number` | `30000` | Idle connections close after this. |
| `atomicRequests` | `boolean` | `true` | Every action that is not `readOnly` (and not `rules.atomic: false`) runs in one lazy transaction. |
| `slowQueryMs` | `number` | `500` | A statement slower than this logs a `warn` on logger `tvine.db` with its SQL (never its params). `0` turns it off. |

Related settings: `settings.data.defaultPageSize` / `maxPageSize` (page sizes for generic views; the QuerySet's own `page()` uses 25 / 100), `settings.encryption` (keys for encrypted fields), `settings.auth.userModel`. See [settings.md](settings.md).

## Environment

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | The database URL when `settings.db.url` is not set. Required by the scaffolded `config/settings/prod.ts`. |

`tvine startproject --db sqlite|postgres|mysql` writes the matching `DATABASE_URL` into `.env` and adds `pg` / `mysql2` to `package.json`.

## Connections

There is one connection handler per process (`connections`, on `globalThis` so the Next.js page bundle shares it). The server configures it from settings at boot; you rarely touch it.

| Function | Signature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `configureDb` | `configureDb(url?: string): void` | Point the default connection at `url` (or `DATABASE_URL`, or the default). Closes any open connection. Opens nothing yet. For scripts and tests. |
| `closeDb` | `closeDb(): void` | Close every open connection (pool `end()`, SQLite `close()`). |

Only the `default` alias is configurable from settings. Not covered: several database aliases / database routers.

Pool stats (`size`, `idle`, `waiting`) appear on `/tvine/health` for Postgres / MySQL. Per-statement duration goes to `/tvine/metrics` as `tvine_db_query_duration_seconds` (labels `db`, `op`) when metrics are enabled.

## Transactions on each engine

- SQLite: one writer. Every ORM operation waits its turn in a process-wide queue; inside `atomic()` the block owns the connection and its queries skip the queue. Keep blocks short; a block that awaits slow I/O holds every other query.
- Postgres / MySQL: plain queries run in parallel on the pool; `atomic()` takes one connection for its whole block.
- A query issued from an `atomic()` callback after the block ended throws `query after the atomic block was committed` (or `rolled back` / `aborted`).

API: [queryset.md](queryset.md#transactions).

## Test databases

The code has no test-database helper and no `TEST` settings block. What it supports:

- Point `DATABASE_URL` (or `settings.db.url`) at a throwaway database, run `tvine migrate` on it, then boot the server or run ORM code. The server never creates tables.
- `:memory:` SQLite is one database per connection: `tvine migrate` (another process) and `migrate(url, ...)` (opens and closes its own connection for a URL string) each migrate a different, throwaway in-memory database. Use a temp file (`file:/tmp/x/test.db`).
- `migrate(url, appsDir, { installed })` can run migrations in-process against the same URL.

```ts
import { mkdtempSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { configureDb, closeDb, migrate } from 'tvine'

const url = `file:${join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'shop-')), 'test.db')}`
await migrate(url, './apps', { installed: ['tvine.auth', 'shop'] })
configureDb(url)
// ... ORM calls ...
closeDb()
```

`warp/src/data/adapters/memory.ts` (`memorySource(items)`) is an in-process array data source for demos and internal tests. It is not exported from `tvine`; models always use the SQL engine.

## Examples

SQLite in development, Postgres in production:

```ts
// config/settings/dev.ts
import { defineSettings } from 'tvine'
import { base } from './base.ts'

export default defineSettings({
  ...base,
  debug: true,
  db: { url: 'file:./tvine.db', slowQueryMs: 200 },
})
```

```ts
// config/settings/prod.ts
import { defineSettings } from 'tvine'
import { base } from './base.ts'

export default defineSettings({
  ...base,
  debug: false,
  db: { pool: { max: 20, acquireMs: 2_000, idleMs: 30_000 } },   // url comes from DATABASE_URL
})
```

```bash
DATABASE_URL=postgres://shop:secret@db.internal:5432/shop tvine migrate
DATABASE_URL='mysql://shop:secret@db.internal:3306/shop?sslmode=require' tvine start
```

A script outside the server:

```ts
import { configureDb, closeDb } from 'tvine'
import { Product } from './apps/shop/models.ts'

configureDb(process.env.DATABASE_URL)
const n = await Product.objects.filter({ stock: 0 }).update({ active: false })
console.log(`${n} products hidden`)
closeDb()
```

Turning off the per-request transaction for one action (rules: [actions.md](actions.md)):

```ts
// apps/shop/views.ts
import { z } from 'zod'
import { defineAction } from 'tvine'
import { Product } from './models.ts'

// each write commits on its own; a failure halfway keeps the rows already written
export const restockAll = defineAction('restockAll', z.object({ amount: z.number().int().min(1) }), async ({ amount }) => {
  const ids = await Product.objects.filter({ active: true }).valuesList('id', { flat: true }).fetchAll() as number[]
  for (const id of ids) await Product.objects.filter({ id }).update({ stock: amount })
  return { updated: ids.length }
}, { atomic: false })
```

## Gotchas

- Postgres and MySQL drivers are optional: install `pg` or `mysql2`, or the first query fails with `install pg to use postgres:// urls`.
- `DATABASE_URL=""` (set but empty) throws on purpose.
- On SQLite, one long `atomic()` block blocks every other query in the process.
- MySQL stores and compares text with `utf8mb4_bin` (exact, case-sensitive equality, like SQLite / Postgres); the case-insensitive lookups lower both sides.
- `configureDb()` closes open connections; do not call it while requests are running.
- The ORM never creates tables; run `tvine migrate`.

## See also

- [migrations.md](migrations.md) — schema changes per engine
- [queryset.md](queryset.md) — `atomic`, `onCommit`, `selectForUpdate`
- [fields.md](fields.md) — column types per engine
- [settings.md](settings.md) — the whole settings object
- [overview.md](overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/actions.md

# Actions (`defineAction`)

An action is one named backend function with a zod schema for its params. You export it from
`apps/<app>/views.ts`; at boot Warp discovers it and gives it the id `<app>.<name>`. From then on the same
action answers everywhere: the typed `api.<app>.<name>()` client in your pages, `POST /tvine/api/<app>.<name>`,
an agent's `POST` to a page, the MCP `do` tool and its own typed MCP tool, and any `urls.ts` path you map to it.
Every caller goes through one pipeline (`core/dispatch.ts`): origin check, rate limits, session, `humanOnly`,
permissions, bind, rev, action middleware, validation, `confirm`, the handler in one DB transaction, commit.

**Import:** `import { defineAction, DomainError, type ActionCtx, type ActionRules } from 'tvine'`

## Signature

```ts
function defineAction<S extends z.ZodType, R = unknown>(
  name: string,
  schema: S,
  run: (params: z.infer<S>, ctx: ActionCtx) => Promise<R>,
  rules?: ActionRules,
): ActionDef<S> & { run(params: z.infer<S>, ctx: ActionCtx): Promise<R> }
```

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Bare name (`'addToCart'`) or already qualified with its own app (`'cart.addToCart'`). A dotted name must start with the app folder's name, or boot fails. |
| `schema` | zod schema | The params. Use `z.object({...})`: only an object schema gets advertised params (MCP tool input, snapshot param specs). |
| `run` | `async (params, ctx) => result` | The handler. `params` is the parsed zod output (defaults filled, unknown keys stripped unless the schema is `.strict()`). The return value is the result. |
| `rules` | `ActionRules` | Optional. Every key below. |

The returned object is the action definition. After discovery its `id` property holds the final id
(`'cart.addToCart'`), so `import { addToCart } from './views.ts'` sees the qualified id.

## Ids

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Id form | `<app>.<name>`. `<app>` is the folder under `apps/` and must match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/`. |
| Where they are found | Every export of `apps/<app>/views.ts` (or `.js` / `.mjs`; two of them side by side is a boot error) that is an action def or a View class. |
| Duplicates | Two actions with the same id fail at boot (`duplicate id cart.addToCart`), naming the file and export. |
| Reserved | The app name `weft` is reserved for framework built-ins. |
| Same name in two apps | Works on the server. A page bundle that resolves the id by bare name throws "defined by several apps"; give it the qualified name: `defineAction('cart.add', …)`. |
| Installed apps | Project apps come from `apps/`; built-ins (`tvine.auth`, …) register under their label (`auth.login`). See [settings.md](./settings.md) `installedApps`. |

## The handler context (`ActionCtx`)

```ts
interface ActionCtx {
  request: Request        // path, query, headers, ip, user, agent, locale, files, raw — see request.md
  session: Session        // { sid, rev, data: Map<string, unknown>, createdAt, lastSeen }
  sid: Sid                // same as session.sid
  settings: Settings      // the validated settings
  channels: ChannelLayer  // pub/sub; sends are held until commit, dropped on rollback
}
```

| Field | What you use it for |
|---|---|
| `ctx.request.user` | The signed-in user, always present (`ANONYMOUS` = `{ isAuthenticated: false, isAnonymous: true }`). |
| `ctx.request.agent` | `{ is, via, client?, verified? }`: is an AI agent calling? See [request.md](./request.md). |
| `ctx.request.ip` | Client IP, derived with `settings.trustProxy`. |
| `ctx.session.data` | Per-session state (a cart). The handler gets a deep copy; it is saved only if the action succeeds. |
| `ctx.channels.group(name).send(event)` | Push an event to a group; delivered after commit only. |
| `ctx.settings` | Read settings at run time. |
