`currentAction()` (in `core/dispatch.ts`, not exported from `tvine`) returns the running `ActionCtx`; it is used
internally by `tvine.tasks`. Not covered as public API.

Class-view methods get a `ViewCtx` instead: the same fields plus `action`, `actionId`, `params`. See [views.md](./views.md).

## Return values

| Handler does | Caller gets |
|---|---|
| returns a value | `ok` with that value as the result. Over `api.*` / `/tvine/api`: `{ ok: true, data }` (JSON round-tripped: a `Date` becomes a string, `undefined` becomes `null`). |
| returns nothing | `{ ok: true, data: null }` |
| throws `DomainError(code, message, field?)` | `err` with code `domain` and `reason: code` (except codes `invalid_param`, `internal`, `human_only`, which keep their own code). See [errors.md](./errors.md). |
| throws Next's `redirect('/orders/42')` | `goto` to that path (the action still commits). The target must be http(s), this site's host, and a routed page; else `domain` / `forbidden`. `api.*` returns `{ ok: true, data: null, goto: '/orders/42' }`. |
| throws anything else | `internal` ("internal error"), logged on `tvine`; the transaction rolls back. |
| runs longer than `settings.limits.handlerMs` (10 s) | `internal` ("handler timeout"); the transaction is aborted. |

## Rules (`ActionRules`)

The fourth argument. Every key:

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | A read. No DB transaction, no session `rev` bump. Allowed while a page renders (`api.*` in a server component); reachable by `GET` in `urls.ts`; MCP `readOnlyHint`; token scope `read` covers it; required by `cache`. |
| `destructive` | `boolean` | `false` | MCP `destructiveHint` (ignored when `readOnly`). The typed tool description says "(destructive)". |
| `permissions` | `Permission[]` | `[]` | Checked before params are validated. First deny wins; a throwing permission is a deny. Merged: `apps/<app>/rules.ts` permissions first, then the action's. Built-ins: `allowAny`, `denyAgents`, `isAuthenticated`, `isStaff`, `isSuperuser`, `hasPerm(...)`, `modelPermissions(Model)`, `allOf`, `anyOf`, `loginRequired`, `permissionRequired`, `userPassesTest`, `staffMemberRequired` (see [contrib/auth.md](./contrib/auth.md)). Denied → `domain` / `forbidden`. |
| `rate` | `{ limit: number; windowMs: number }` | `settings.limits.rate` (60 / 60 s) | The action's own bucket, keyed by session + action id. `limit >= 1`, `windowMs > 0`, else boot error. Over it → `rate_limited` + `retryAfterMs`. |
| `mcp` | `boolean` | `true` (unless matched by `settings.mcp.exclude`) | `false`: no typed MCP tool, refused by the MCP `do` tool (answers `unknown_action`), hidden from MCP snapshots. Other transports still work. |
| `priority` | `boolean` | `false` | Kept when the typed MCP tool list is trimmed to `settings.mcp.maxTools`. |
| `humanOnly` | `true \| string` | unset | Every agent-marked request gets `human_only` (HTTP 403), before replay and permissions. The string is shown in the message. No typed MCP tool. A human's own request runs it. |
| `confirm` | `true \| { message?, by? } \| (params, ctx) => rule \| undefined` | unset | Two-step call. First call runs nothing and returns `confirm_required` with a signed, single-use token (bound to sid + action + params, valid 120 s). Same call again with `params.$confirm = token` runs it. `message`: a string or `(params, ctx) => string` (default `Confirm <id>?`). `by: 'human'`: an agent never gets a token and cannot confirm. A function decides per call. |
| `bind` | `string[]` | `[]` | Params that may only come from the server-signed `bind` token of an action ref (never from the caller). With `bind` set, a call without a bind → `stale_bind`; sending one of these keys as a param → `invalid_param`. Each key must be a param of the schema (boot error otherwise). Not advertised as params or MCP inputs. |
| `atomic` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` opts out of the per-action DB transaction (`settings.db.atomicRequests`). |
| `cache` | `{ timeout: number; varyOn?: string[]; cache?: string; tags?: string[] }` | unset | Caches the result. Needs `readOnly` (boot error otherwise), `timeout` in seconds > 0, not with `secretResult`. `varyOn` default `['user']`; add `'session'`, `'query'` or a header name. `cache`: the `settings.caches` alias. `tags`: dropped by `cache.invalidateTags([...])`. Errors are never cached. |
| `secretResult` | `boolean` | `false` | The result is a one-time secret (a new API token): blanked as `[redacted]` in hook payloads. Not allowed with `cache`. |
| `audit` | `boolean` | `true` | `false`: never write a `tvine.audit` row for this action (when `settings.audit.enabled`). |
| `search` | `string` | unset | Names the param that is a visitor's search term (admin "Top searches"). Generated `list` actions set `'q'` when the view has search fields. |
| `anonymous` | `boolean` | — | Declared in the type ("default true in v1"); nothing reads it in this release. |
| `humanAttention` | `true \| string` | — | Reserved placeholder; no behaviour on the server. |

### Where rules come from (precedence)

`settings.limits.rate` < the def's own defaults (e.g. `defineUpload`'s 5/min) < `apps/<app>/rules.ts` < the
action's `rules`. `apps/<app>/rules.ts` may export only `rate`, `mcp` and `permissions`; permissions add up
(app first), the others are overridden by the action.

```ts
// apps/orders/rules.ts — applies to every action of the orders app
import { isAuthenticated } from 'tvine'
export const permissions = [isAuthenticated]
export const rate = { limit: 30, windowMs: 60_000 }
```

## How one action is reachable

| Caller | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Page (server component) | `await api.cart.addToCart({ productId: 7, qty: 1 })` from `tvine/api` | In-process. During a render only `readOnly` actions run (`domain` / `render_mutation` otherwise). |
| Page (client component) | same call | `POST /tvine/api/cart.addToCart` with the session cookie. |
| Any HTTP client | `POST /tvine/api/cart.addToCart`, body `{ "params": {...}, "bind"?, "cmdId"? }`, header `x-tvine-api: 1` | Same-origin (or `settings.cors`). See [request.md](./request.md). |
| Agent over HTTP | `POST <page url>` with header `x-tvine: 1`, body `{ "action": "cart.addToCart", "params": {...}, "sid": "...", "bind"?, "cmdId"?, "rev"? }` | Reply is a snapshot envelope (json / notation). |
| MCP | typed tool `cart_addToCart` (dots → `_`) with the params plus `url`, `sid`, `cmdId`, `bind`; or `do` with `{ url, action, params, sid }` | Server at `POST /mcp`. |
| REST | a `urls.ts` route: `path('api/cart/add/', addToCart)` | See [urls.md](./urls.md). |

### The typed `api.*` client

`api` is a proxy: `api.<app>.<name>(params?, opts?)` calls id `<app>.<name>` and **never throws**; it returns

```ts
type ApiResult<T> =
  | { ok: true; data: T; goto?: string }
  | { ok: false; code: ErrCode; reason?: string; field?: string; errors?: FieldError[];
      message: string; retryAfterMs?: number; confirm?: ConfirmAsk }
```

`opts`: `{ cmdId?: string; bind?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }`. `must(r)` returns `data` or throws
`ApiError`; `must(r, { notFound: true })` turns `reason: 'not_found'` into Next's 404. In the browser a
`confirm_required` answer shows a confirm dialog and resends with the token (agents get the result instead).

Types: `tvine generate` writes `tvine-api.d.ts`, which types each call from the action's zod input
(`z.input`) and the handler's return type (`ActionIn` / `ActionOut` from `tvine/types`). `tvine dev`
regenerates it on save; `tvine generate --check` fails when it is stale.

### MCP tool details

| Point | Detail |
|---|---|
| Name | id with `.` replaced by `_` (`catalog.list` → `catalog_list`). |
| Input schema | The zod schema as JSON Schema, minus `bind` keys, plus `url`, `sid`, `cmdId`, `bind`. Skipped (warning, still reachable by `do`) when the schema is not an object, a param is named `url`/`sid`/`cmdId`/`bind`, or the name is taken. |
| Hints | `readOnlyHint` = `readOnly`; `destructiveHint` = `destructive && !readOnly`. |
| Hidden | `mcp: false`, `settings.mcp.exclude` globs (`*` one segment, `**` any depth), `humanOnly`, or a permission list containing `isStaff`, `isSuperuser` or `denyAgents`. Hidden typed tools are still enforced on every path. |
| Mode | `settings.mcp.tools`: `'both'` (default; 6 generic tools + typed), `'generic'`, `'typed'`. |
| Trim | Over `settings.mcp.maxTools` (40), typed tools are cut to `priority` ones; the rest work through `do`. |

## Idempotency, rev, bind

| Field (command) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cmdId` | Idempotency key. A retry with the same `cmdId` and same params replays the first result, never runs twice. Same `cmdId`, different params → `conflict`. `/tvine/api`: body `cmdId`; `urls.ts`: header `Idempotency-Key`. Ignored on throwaway sessions (anonymous reads). |
| `rev` | Optimistic concurrency: if given and not the session's current rev → `stale_rev` + fresh snapshot. |
| `bind` | Opaque HMAC-signed context from an action ref. Must be valid and issued for this action, else `stale_bind`. Its values are merged over the params. |

## Action middleware

Functions around the handler, for every action (`settings.actionMiddleware`) or one app's actions
(`apps/<app>/middleware.ts`, `export default [fn, ...]`). Global ones run first.

```ts
type Middleware = (cmd: Command, ctx: ActionCtx, next: () => AsyncIterable<Event>) => AsyncIterable<Event>
```

They run after the origin check, rate limits, session, `humanOnly`, permissions, bind and rev checks, and
before param validation, `confirm` and the handler. `cmd` is frozen. Yield your own `err` event to stop;
`yield* next()` to continue; `next()` at most once. Full detail: [middleware.md](./middleware.md#action-middleware).

## Examples

### 1. A cart action using the session

```ts
// apps/cart/views.ts
import { z } from 'zod'
import { defineAction, DomainError } from 'tvine'
import { Product } from '../catalog/models.ts'

export const addToCart = defineAction('addToCart',
  z.object({ productId: z.number().int(), qty: z.number().int().min(1).max(99) }),
  async ({ productId, qty }, ctx) => {
    const p = await Product.objects.filter({ id: productId }).first()
    if (!p) throw new DomainError('not_found', `product ${productId} not found`, 'productId')
    const cart = (ctx.session.data.get('cart') as Record<number, number> | undefined) ?? {}
    cart[productId] = (cart[productId] ?? 0) + qty
    ctx.session.data.set('cart', cart)
    return { lines: Object.keys(cart).length }
  },
  { rate: { limit: 20, windowMs: 60_000 } })          // → cart.addToCart, tool cart_addToCart
```

### 2. A cached read

```ts
export const featured = defineAction('featured', z.object({ limit: z.number().int().max(20).default(8) }),
  async ({ limit }) => Product.objects.filter({ featured: true }).order('-createdAt').page({ size: limit }),
  { readOnly: true, cache: { timeout: 60, varyOn: [], tags: ['products'] } })   // one copy for everyone
```

### 3. A confirmed, human-only refund

```ts
import { isStaff } from 'tvine'

export const refund = defineAction('refund', z.object({ orderId: z.number().int() }),
  async ({ orderId }) => { /* ... */ return { refunded: orderId } },
  { permissions: [isStaff], destructive: true,
    confirm: { message: (p) => `Refund order ${p.orderId}?`, by: 'human' } })
```

### 4. Calling it from a page

```tsx
import { api, must } from 'tvine/api'

const r = await api.cart.addToCart({ productId: 7, qty: 2 })
if (!r.ok) setError(r.field ?? 'form', r.message)        // client component: never throws
const items = must(await api.catalog.featured({}))         // server component: data or ApiError
```

### 5. Redirect after placing an order

```ts
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'

export const place = defineAction('place', z.object({}), async (_p, ctx) => {
  const order = await createOrderFromCart(ctx)              // your code
  ctx.session.data.delete('cart')
  redirect(`/orders/${order.id}`)                           // → goto; must be a routed page of this site
})
```

## Gotchas

- `/tvine/api` params go under `params`. Top-level keys are ignored.
- A page render may only call `readOnly` actions; a write during render returns `domain` / `render_mutation`.
- `ctx.session.data` writes are applied only when the action succeeds. Writes made by middleware after `next()`
  returned are outside the commit.
- `confirm` is opt-in per action; `$confirm` is stripped from params before your handler and never validated.
- Rules on an action override `rules.ts` for `rate` and `mcp`; `permissions` always add up.
- A permission is checked before params are validated, so it cannot read validated params.
- `bind` keys must be in the schema, or boot fails.
- `rules.cache` without `readOnly` is a boot error.
- `humanOnly` cannot be overridden by any rule, permission or hook.

## See also

[views.md](./views.md) · [errors.md](./errors.md) · [request.md](./request.md) · [middleware.md](./middleware.md) ·
[urls.md](./urls.md) · [serializers.md](./serializers.md) · [settings.md](./settings.md) · [contrib/auth.md](./contrib/auth.md) ·
[overview.md](./overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/views.md

# Class views, ViewSets, `@action` and routers

Class views are generic CRUD views. You export a class from
`apps/<app>/views.ts`; at boot Warp creates it once, checks its config against the model, and turns it into
ordinary actions: `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete` (whichever the base class generates) plus one action
per `@action` method. Those actions are registered exactly like `defineAction` ones (same ids, rules, MCP tools,
`api.*` calls, pipeline). Every call runs on a fresh `Object.create(view)`, so `this.x = …` never leaks between
requests. Routers (`SimpleRouter`) map a view's actions to REST URLs.

**Import:** `import { ListView, DetailView, ModelViewSet, action, defineSerializer, View, GenericView, type ViewCtx } from 'tvine'`
and `import { SimpleRouter, DefaultRouter } from 'tvine'` for routers.

## Base classes

| Class | Generated actions |
|---|---|
| `View` | none (only `@action` methods) |
| `GenericView` | none (`static actions = []`; set it yourself) |
| `ListView` | `list` |
| `DetailView` | `get` |
| `CreateView` | `create` |
| `UpdateView` | `update` |
| `DeleteView` | `delete` |
| `ListCreateView` | `list`, `create` |
| `RetrieveUpdateView` | `get`, `update` |
| `RetrieveDestroyView` | `get`, `delete` |
| `RetrieveUpdateDestroyView` | `get`, `update`, `delete` |
| `ModelViewSet` | `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete` |

## Ids of generated actions

The action name is the generated name: a `ListView` in `apps/catalog/` gives `catalog.list`. When two view
classes in one app generate the same name, both become `<ExportName>.<name>`: `catalog.ProductList.list`,
`catalog.CategoryList.list`. `@action` methods are named after the method (`catalog.addToCart`), with the same
collision rule.

## Generated actions

| Action | Params | Rules | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `q?` (when there are search fields), `sort?` (when `ordering` is set), `cursor?` or `page?`, one optional param per filter | `readOnly`, `search: 'q'` when searchable | `Paginated` (below), items serialized |
| `get` | `{ [lookupParam]: value }` (strict) | `readOnly` | the serialized object |
| `create` | the serializer input (strict) | — | the serialized new object (HTTP 201 through `urls.ts`) |
| `update` | `{ [lookupParam] }` + the serializer input, all optional (partial, strict) | — | the serialized object |
| `delete` | `{ [lookupParam] }` (strict) | `destructive` | `null` |

Missing object (or scoped out by `getQueryset`) → `DomainError('not_found', '<Model> <id> not found')` →
`domain` / `not_found` (HTTP 404).

List result:

```ts
// pagination 'cursor' (default)
{ items: Row[], pageSize: number, nextCursor?: string, total?: number }   // QuerySet.page(); pass nextCursor as ?cursor=
// pagination 'page'
{ items: Row[], total: number, pageSize: number, page: number, numPages: number }
```

## Options (instance fields)

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | `Model` | required (boot error "needs `model = SomeModel`") | The `defineModel` model. |
| `lookupField` | `string` | `'id'` | DRF `lookup_field`: the model field `get`/`update`/`delete` filter on. Must exist. |
| `lookupParam` | `string` | `'id'` | DRF `lookup_url_kwarg`: the param name carrying the lookup value. If the lookup field is writable in `update`, boot fails: set `lookupParam` to something else (e.g. `'key'`) or list it in `readOnlyFields`. |
| `serializer` | `Serializer<T>` | model default | `defineSerializer({ input?, readOnlyFields?, output })`. See [serializers.md](./serializers.md). |
| `permissions` | `Permission[]` | `[]` | Checked per call by `checkPermissions` (before params are validated). Ones that deny agents (`denyAgents`) are also copied into the action rules (MCP hiding), unless you override `getPermissions`. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `25` | Page size (capped by `maxPageSize`). |
| `maxPageSize` | `number` | `100` | Upper cap. |
| `pagination` | `'cursor' \| 'page'` | `'cursor'` | `'cursor'`: keyset, stable under inserts. `'page'`: page numbers, `?page=N`. |
| `filters` | `string[]` | the model's enum fields and indexed fields (never hidden / writeOnly) | Field lookups allowed as params: `'status'`, `'price__lte'`, `'tags__in'`, `'name__contains'`. Suffixes: exact, `__lt`, `__lte`, `__gt`, `__gte`, `__in` (comma list or array), `__contains` (text/email/url/slug only, max 200 chars), `__ne`. Unknown field or suffix → boot error. |
| `searchFields` | `string[]` | the model's `searchable` fields | Fields `?q=` searches (max 200 chars). A money field cannot be searched. |
| `ordering` | `string[]` | `[]` | Allowed `sort` values; each also allowed as `-field` (descending). |
| `shapers` | `Shapers` | from `apps/<app>/serializers.ts` | Set by discovery; output shapers by model name. See [serializers.md](./serializers.md). |

### Static fields

| Static | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `static permissions` | `Permission[]` | Merged into the rules of every action of the class (checked by dispatch, visible to MCP hiding). |
| `static actions` | `readonly GeneratedAction[]` | Which of `list/get/create/update/delete` to generate (set by the base classes). |

### Param coercion

Filter and lookup values may arrive as URL strings; they are coerced by field type: `"30"` → `30` for
int/float/id/duration, `"true"`/`"false"` for bool, ISO strings → `Date` for datetime, money in major units
(`"30"` = 30.00, max 2 decimals), `"a,b"` → array for `__in`. An empty string is treated as absent.

## Hooks you can override

Names follow DRF, camelCase. `ctx` is a `ViewCtx` (`ActionCtx` + `action`, `actionId`, `params`).

| Hook | Default | Override to |
|---|---|---|
| `getQueryset(ctx)` | `this.model.objects` | Scope rows to the user / tenant. Every list/get/update/delete read goes through it. |
| `filterQueryset(qs, ctx)` | applies filters, `q`, `sort` | Add custom filtering. |
| `paginateQueryset(qs, ctx)` | cursor or page pagination | Change paging. |
| `getObject(ctx)` | scoped + filtered + lookup, `not_found` if none, then `checkObjectPermissions` | Custom lookup. |
| `getPermissions(ctx)` | `this.permissions` | Per-action permissions. |
| `checkPermissions(ctx)` | runs `getPermissions` | — |
| `checkObjectPermissions(ctx, obj)` | allow | Throw `DomainError('forbidden', …)` to deny (DRF `has_object_permission`). |
| `getSerializer(ctx)` | `this.serializer` or the model default | Pick a serializer per action. The advertised create/update schema is read at boot with `ctx.action` set and an anonymous user. |
| `getSerializerContext(ctx)` | `{ request, user, view, action }` | Extra data for `output(obj, sctx)`. |
| `performCreate(data, ctx)` | `model.create(data)` | Set owner, side effects. |
| `performUpdate(obj, data, ctx)` | `model.update(obj.id, data)` (no-op if `data` empty) | — |
| `performDestroy(obj, ctx)` | `model.delete(obj.id)` | Soft delete. |

Order per call: permissions → validate params → hooks → serializer output.

## `@action`

```ts
function action<S extends z.ZodType>(schema: S, opts?: {
  rules?: ActionRules          // any defineAction rule
  permissions?: Permission[]   // extra permissions for this action
  detail?: boolean             // routers: true = on /<prefix>/<id>/<name>/
  methods?: string[]           // routers: HTTP methods
}): MethodDecorator
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rules` | `{}` | Same keys as [actions.md](./actions.md#rules-actionrules). |
| `permissions` | `[]` | Added to the static and instance permissions. |
| `detail` | `true` when the schema has the view's `lookupParam` | Router URL shape. |
| `methods` | `['GET']` if `rules.readOnly`, else `['POST']` | Router methods. `GET` on a non-readOnly action is a boot error in `urls.ts`. |

The method must be public, non-static, string-named. `this` is the view (a per-call copy), so
`this.getObject(ctx)` and `this.getQueryset(ctx)` work. On a `GenericView`, `checkPermissions` runs first.
Works with TC39 decorators, the 2018-09 form (Next's SWC) and `experimentalDecorators`.

## Page helpers (static)

| Helper | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `View.asAction(name)` / `View.action(name)` | the registered `ActionDef` | For `<Form action={ProductDetail.asAction('addToCart')}>` or `path('x/', ProductDetail.action('addToCart'))`. Throws if the view was not discovered. |
| `await ListViewClass.queryset(searchParams, ctx?)` | the same `Paginated` as `<app>.list` | Unknown or invalid URL keys are dropped (a hand-edited URL never 500s). Without `ctx`, hooks see `ANONYMOUS`. |
| `await DetailViewClass.object(id, { request? })` | serialized object or `undefined` | `undefined` for `not_found` / `forbidden`; call `notFound()`. |

## Routers

```ts
class SimpleRouter {
  constructor(opts?: { trailingSlash?: boolean })            // default true
  register(prefix: string, view: ViewClass, opts?: { basename?: string }): this
  get urls(): UrlEntry[]
}
class DefaultRouter extends SimpleRouter {}                    // same; no API root view
```

| Route | Methods | Name |
|---|---|---|
| `<prefix>/` | `GET` → `list`, `POST` → `create` | `<basename>-list` |
| `<prefix>/<id>/` | `GET` → `get`, `PUT`/`PATCH` → `update`, `DELETE` → `delete` | `<basename>-detail` |
| `<prefix>/<id>/<name>/` | `@action` with `detail: true` | `<basename>-<name>` |
| `<prefix>/<name>/` | `@action` with `detail: false` | `<basename>-<name>` |

`basename` defaults to the lowercased model name. The `<id>` converter is `int` when the lookup field is an id
or int field, else any segment without `/` or `.`. Use `router.urls` in a `urlpatterns` array; see [urls.md](./urls.md).

## Examples

### 1. Product list + detail with an extra action

```ts
// apps/catalog/views.ts
import { z } from 'zod'
import { action, DetailView, ListView, type ViewCtx } from 'tvine'
import { Product } from './models.ts'

export class ProductList extends ListView<Product> {      // → catalog.list
  model = Product
  filters = ['category', 'price__lte', 'tags__in']          // ?category=hats&price__lte=30
  searchFields = ['name', 'description']                  // ?q=wool
  ordering = ['price', 'createdAt']                        // ?sort=-price
  pageSize = 24
}

export class ProductDetail extends DetailView<Product> {  // → catalog.get
  model = Product

  @action(z.object({ id: z.number().int(), qty: z.number().int().min(1) }))
  async addToCart({ id, qty }: { id: number; qty: number }, ctx: ViewCtx) {   // → catalog.addToCart
    const p = await this.getObject(ctx)                    // ctx.params = { id, qty }, validated
    const cart = (ctx.session.data.get('cart') as Record<number, number> | undefined) ?? {}
    cart[p.id] = (cart[p.id] ?? 0) + qty
    ctx.session.data.set('cart', cart)
    return { ok: true }
  }
}
```

### 2. Orders scoped to the signed-in user

```ts
import { isAuthenticated, ListView } from 'tvine'
import { Order } from './models.ts'

export class MyOrders extends ListView<Order> {            // → orders.list
  model = Order
  static permissions = [isAuthenticated]
  pagination = 'page' as const
  ordering = ['createdAt']
  getQueryset(ctx) { return Order.objects.filter({ customer: ctx.request.user.id }) }
}
```

### 3. A ViewSet with owner set on create and a router

```ts
// apps/catalog/views.ts
import { defineSerializer, DomainError, ModelViewSet } from 'tvine'
import { Review } from './models.ts'

export class ReviewViewSet extends ModelViewSet<Review> {
  model = Review
  serializer = defineSerializer<Review>({ readOnlyFields: ['author'], output: (r) => ({ id: r.id, stars: r.stars, text: r.text }) })
  performCreate(data, ctx) { return Review.create({ ...data, author: ctx.request.user.id }) }
  async checkObjectPermissions(ctx, obj) {
    if (ctx.action !== 'get' && obj.author !== ctx.request.user.id) throw new DomainError('forbidden', 'not your review')
  }
}

// apps/catalog/urls.ts
import { SimpleRouter } from 'tvine'
import { ReviewViewSet } from './views.ts'
const router = new SimpleRouter().register('reviews', ReviewViewSet)
export const appName = 'catalog'
export const urlpatterns = router.urls     // /reviews/ and /reviews/<int:id>/
```

### 4. Server component using the helpers

```tsx
// app/shop/page.tsx
import { ProductList } from '@/apps/catalog/views'
export default async function Shop({ searchParams }) {
  const page = await ProductList.queryset(await searchParams)     // same data as api.catalog.list
  return <ul>{page.items.map((p) => <li key={String(p.id)}>{String(p.name)}</li>)}</ul>
}
```

(Pages should normally call `api.catalog.list(...)`; importing a view class that imports models may trip the
FE/DB boundary check in `tvine check`.)

## Gotchas

- A view class is instantiated once at boot; per-request state on `this` is per call (a fresh copy), not shared.
- `filters` default to the model's enum and indexed fields: set `filters = []` to turn filtering off.
- Every list/get/update/delete read goes through `getQueryset`; scope there, not in `filterQueryset`.
- `update` is always partial; `create` input comes from the serializer (or the model minus read-only fields).
- `serializer.input` must be a plain `z.object(...)` (no `.refine` on the object), or boot fails.
- Switching serializers per request works at run time but the advertised schema (MCP, types) is the boot one.
- Unknown params are rejected (`invalid_param`, "unknown param"); sending a read-only field gives code `read_only`.
- Two classes generating the same action name in one app get prefixed ids (`catalog.ProductList.list`).

## See also

[actions.md](./actions.md) · [serializers.md](./serializers.md) · [urls.md](./urls.md) · [errors.md](./errors.md) ·
[models.md](./models.md) · [contrib/auth.md](./contrib/auth.md) · [overview.md](./overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/serializers.md

# Serializers

A serializer decides two things for a class view: what a caller may send to `create` / `update` (a zod object)
and what each row looks like on the way out (a plain function). It is DRF's `ModelSerializer` reduced to those
two jobs. Without one, a view derives both from its model: input = the model's writable fields, output = every
field except `hidden` and `writeOnly` ones. A second, lighter tool, `apps/<app>/serializers.ts`, reshapes the
default output per model without writing a full serializer. Plain `defineAction` actions have no serializer:
their zod schema is the input and their return value is the output.

**Import:** `import { defineSerializer, type Serializer } from 'tvine'`

## Signature

```ts
interface Serializer<T> {
  input?: z.ZodObject<z.ZodRawShape>                  // create / update params
  readOnlyFields?: string[]                           // DRF read_only_fields
  output(obj: T, sctx: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown>
}
const defineSerializer = <T>(s: Serializer<T>): Serializer<T> => s   // identity, for typing
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | `z.object({...})` | the model's create input (below) | The params of `create`; `update` uses `input.partial()` plus the lookup param. Must be a plain `z.object`: a refined / transformed object is a boot error ("must be a plain z.object(...)"); refine individual fields instead. |
| `readOnlyFields` | `string[]` | `[]` | Removed from the input. A caller sending one gets `invalid_param` with field code `read_only` ("`"x" is read-only`"). Added to the model's own read-only set. |
| `output` | `(obj, sctx) => object` | required | Builds the result for one row. `sctx` = `getSerializerContext(ctx)`: `{ request, user, view, action }`. |

The final input schema is `input.omit(readOnly).strict()`: unknown keys are rejected (field code `unknown`,
"unknown param"). Validation errors list every bad field (`errors[]`), see [errors.md](./errors.md).

## The default serializer (no `serializer` set)

| Part | Rule |
|---|---|
| Input fields | Every model field except: `id` / `uuid` primary keys, fields with `auto`, `autoNow` or `autoNowAdd`, fields with `readOnly`, fields with `hidden` (unless also `writeOnly`), and `m2m` fields (written through `Model.related()`). |
| Optional | A field that is `optional`, has a `default`, or is auto is optional in `create`. All fields are optional in `update`. |
| Output | The row object minus `hidden` and `writeOnly` fields. |
| Shaper | If `apps/<app>/serializers.ts` exports a shaper for this model, it is applied to that output. |

Field options (`readOnly`, `writeOnly`, `hidden`, `searchable`, `index`, `humanOnly`, defaults) live on the
model fields: see [models.md](./models.md).

## `apps/<app>/serializers.ts` (shapers)

```ts
// apps/catalog/serializers.ts
export const serializers = {
  Product: (row) => ({ ...row, priceLabel: `$${(row.price as { value: number }).value}` }),
}
```

| Point | Detail |
|---|---|
| Export | `serializers`: a record keyed by **model name** → `(row) => row`. |
| Applies to | The default serializer's output of class views in the same app. A view with its own `serializer` does not use it. |
| Loaded | At discovery, next to `views.ts` (`.ts` / `.js` / `.mjs`). |
| Agent snapshots | `serialize/envelope.ts` can apply shapers by node type, but no transport passes them in this release. Not covered. |

## Relation to zod and the model

| Thing | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `create` params | `serializer.input` (or the model's writable fields), minus `readOnlyFields`, strict |
| `update` params | `{ [lookupParam] }` + the same input `.partial()`, strict |
| `list` params | filters / `q` / `sort` / `cursor` or `page`, built from the view config (not the serializer) |
| Output type in `tvine-api.d.ts` | `Record<string, unknown>` for generated actions (`ViewOut`); `@action` methods are typed by their return type |
| Wire format | JSON (`api.*`, `/tvine/api`): a `Date` arrives as a string |
| Humans-only fields | A field with `humanOnly` refuses agent writes in `create` / `update` with `human_only` (setting it to the value it already has is allowed) |

Nested objects: there is no nested-serializer class. Build nested data in `output` (load related rows in
`getQueryset` with prefetch, then map them). Writable nested input: Not covered.

## Examples

### 1. Public product output

```ts
// apps/catalog/views.ts
import { defineSerializer, DetailView, ListView } from 'tvine'
import { Product } from './models.ts'

const publicProduct = defineSerializer<Product>({
  output: (p) => ({ id: p.id, name: p.name, price: p.price, inStock: p.stock > 0 }),
})

export class ProductList extends ListView<Product> { model = Product; serializer = publicProduct }
export class ProductDetail extends DetailView<Product> { model = Product; serializer = publicProduct }
```

### 2. Limited create input with read-only fields

```ts
import { z } from 'zod'
import { CreateView, defineSerializer } from 'tvine'
import { Review } from './models.ts'

export class ReviewCreate extends CreateView<Review> {
  model = Review
  serializer = defineSerializer<Review>({
    input: z.object({ product: z.number().int(), stars: z.number().int().min(1).max(5), text: z.string().max(2000), author: z.string() }),
    readOnlyFields: ['author'],                       // sending author → invalid_param, code read_only
    output: (r) => ({ id: r.id, stars: r.stars, text: r.text }),
  })
  performCreate(data, ctx) { return Review.create({ ...data, author: ctx.request.user.id }) }
}
```

### 3. Different output per action and user

```ts
export class OrderViewSet extends ModelViewSet<Order> {
  model = Order
  getSerializer(ctx) {
    return defineSerializer<Order>({
      output: (o, sctx) => ({
        id: o.id, status: o.status, total: o.total,
        ...((sctx.user as { isStaff?: boolean }).isStaff && { internalNote: o.note }),
        ...(sctx.action === 'get' && { lines: o.lines }),
      }),
    })
  }
}
```

## Gotchas

- `serializer.input` must be a plain `z.object`; `.refine()` on the object fails at boot.
- `readOnlyFields` names must match input keys; listing a key not in the input just does nothing.
- The advertised (MCP / typed) create and update schemas come from `getSerializer` at boot with an anonymous
  user; a per-request switch does not change them.
- Shapers in `serializers.ts` only touch the default serializer; once you set `serializer`, do the shaping in `output`.
- If `lookupParam` equals a writable field name in `update`, boot fails; rename the param or make the field read-only.
- The serializer's output is not filtered again: anything `output` returns is sent.

## See also

[views.md](./views.md) · [actions.md](./actions.md) · [models.md](./models.md) · [errors.md](./errors.md) ·
[overview.md](./overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/urls.md

# URLs (`urls.ts`, `path`, `include`, `reverse`)

`urls.ts` is the URL table for REST-style paths. It is optional: without it every action still answers at
`POST /tvine/api/<app>.<name>`. Each route maps a URL pattern (and HTTP methods) to an action that discovery
already registered; a matched request runs that action exactly as `POST /tvine/api/<id>` does (same caller
check, permissions, rate limits, idempotency, `humanOnly`, origin / CORS, same JSON result). Pages are not routed
here: pages are your Next.js `app/` folder, and Warp reads that route table itself.

**Import:** `import { path, re_path, include, reverse, SimpleRouter, DefaultRouter, NoReverseMatch, ImproperlyConfigured } from 'tvine'`

## Where the files are

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `config/urls.ts`, else `urls.ts` (project root = the folder above `apps/`) | The root URL table. Exports `urlpatterns`. |
| `settings.rootUrlconf` | Another root, a path from the project root without extension (`'config/api_urls'`). Must exist, else boot error. |
| `apps/<app>/urls.ts` | An app's patterns, pulled in with `include('<app>.urls')`. Exports `urlpatterns` and optionally `appName` (the default namespace). |
| `include('tvine.auth.urls')` | A built-in app's patterns (`tvine.<label>.urls`), when that app is installed. |

`.ts`, `.js` or `.mjs`; two side by side is a boot error. Every problem fails at boot naming its file.

## `path`

```ts
function path(route: string, view: ActionDef | ViewClass | Include, opts?: { name?: string; methods?: string[] }): UrlEntry
```

| Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `route` | `string` | — | Path syntax with converters: `'products/<int:id>/'`. No leading `/` (boot error). Matched against the decoded request path. |
| `view` | action def, `View.action('name')`, a View class, or `include(...)` | — | What runs. |
| `opts.name` | `string` | unset | URL name for `reverse`; prefixed by the namespaces (`'catalog:product-detail'`). |
| `opts.methods` | `string[]` | `['GET']` for a `readOnly` action, else `['POST']` | Methods for an action view. Ignored for a View class (it maps its own). |

A View class as `view`: on a route **with** the view's `lookupParam` → `GET` get,
`PUT`/`PATCH` update, `DELETE` delete; on a route **without** it → `GET` list, `POST` create (whichever the class
generates). A route that maps no method fails at boot.

### Converters

| Converter | Matches | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `str` (default: `<name>`) | one segment, no `/` | string |
| `int` | 1–15 digits | number |
| `slug` | `[-a-zA-Z0-9_]+` | string |
| `uuid` | lowercase hex uuid | string |
| `path` | anything, including `/` | string |

Unknown converter or a parameter name that is not an identifier → `ImproperlyConfigured` at `path()` time.
Custom converters: Not covered (no registration API).

## `re_path`

```ts
function re_path(regex: string, view: ActionDef | ViewClass | Include, opts?: { name?: string; methods?: string[] }): UrlEntry
```

Python named groups `(?P<id>\d+)` are accepted; leading `^` and trailing `$` are stripped. Values arrive as
strings. `re_path` routes cannot be reversed.

## `include`

```ts
function include(module: string | UrlEntry[], opts?: { namespace?: string })
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `module` | `'<app>.urls'` (an installed project app), `'tvine.<label>.urls'` (a built-in), or an array of patterns. |
| `opts.namespace` | Namespace for names inside; defaults to the module's `appName` export. Nested includes join with `:`. |

## `reverse`

```ts
function reverse(name: string, kwargs?: Record<string, string | number>, urls?: UrlTable): string
```

Returns the path (leading `/`) of the first route with that name whose parameters are exactly `kwargs` and whose
converters accept the values. Values are URL-encoded (`path` keeps its `/`). Uses the booted server's table, so
it works from page code once the server runs. Throws `NoReverseMatch` for an unknown name, an unknown namespace,
or kwargs that fit no pattern.

## Routers

`new SimpleRouter({ trailingSlash? }).register(prefix, ViewClass, { basename? }).urls` builds the DRF routes:
`<prefix>/` (list, create), `<prefix>/<id>/` (get, update, delete), and `@action` routes. Names are
`<basename>-list`, `<basename>-detail`, `<basename>-<action>`. Full table: [views.md](./views.md#routers).
`DefaultRouter` is the same as `SimpleRouter` (no API root view).

## How a request on a route is handled

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| Match | Path decoded, then every route tested; the first route that has the request's method wins. Path matched but method not → `405` with `Allow`. `HEAD` = `GET`. |
| Caller | Must send `x-tvine-api: 1` (browsers / HTTP clients) or a valid signed `x-tvine-forward` (a Next server in two-server mode). Else `403`. |
| Params (GET) | The query string; repeated keys become arrays; numbers / booleans coerced by the action's schema. |
| Params (other methods) | The JSON body (an object, `Content-Type: application/json`, max `settings.limits.bodyBytes`, else `413`). Empty body = `{}`. |
| Path params | Merged in; a body / query value that differs from the URL value → `400 invalid_param` ("the URL says …"). |
| Headers | `x-tvine-bind` → bind; `Idempotency-Key` → cmdId. |
| Run | `invoke()` → `dispatch()`: same as `/tvine/api`. |
| Reply | JSON `ApiResult` (`{ ok: true, data }` or `{ ok: false, code, … }`), `cache-control: private, no-store`. `201` for a generated `create`. Error statuses: [errors.md](./errors.md#http-status-codes). |

Boot checks: `GET` mapped to a non-`readOnly` action → error ("GET only reaches readOnly actions"); the same
method + pattern routed twice → error; one name on two different patterns → error.

## Page routes vs API routes

| | Page routes | `urls.ts` routes | `/tvine/api/<id>` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Defined by | Next `app/**/page.tsx` | `urlpatterns` | every action, always |
| Human GET | Next renders HTML | JSON | — (POST only) |
| Agent | `x-tvine: 1` GET → snapshot, POST → command | same JSON | same JSON |
| Guards | `settings.guards` by page path | the caller's page is the Referer path | same |

`tvine show_urls` prints every `urls.ts` route: pattern, methods, name, action.

## Examples

### 1. Root URLconf with an app include

```ts
// config/urls.ts
import { include, path } from 'tvine'
export const urlpatterns = [
  path('api/', include('catalog.urls')),
  path('api/auth/', include('tvine.auth.urls')),
]
```

### 2. App patterns: function action, view class, `@action`

```ts
// apps/catalog/urls.ts
import { path } from 'tvine'
import { featured, ProductDetail, ProductList } from './views.ts'

export const appName = 'catalog'
export const urlpatterns = [
  path('products/', ProductList, { name: 'product-list' }),                       // GET → catalog.list
  path('products/<int:id>/', ProductDetail, { name: 'product-detail' }),          // GET → catalog.get
  path('products/<int:id>/add/', ProductDetail.action('addToCart'), { name: 'add' }),   // POST
  path('featured/', featured, { name: 'featured' }),                              // GET (readOnly)
]
```

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/products/?category=hats -H 'x-tvine-api: 1'
# {"ok":true,"data":{"items":[...],"pageSize":25}}
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/products/7/add/ -H 'x-tvine-api: 1' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'Idempotency-Key: k-123' -d '{"qty":2}'
```

### 3. Reverse a URL

```ts
import { reverse } from 'tvine'
reverse('catalog:product-detail', { id: 7 })   // '/api/products/7/'
```

### 4. Router

```ts
// apps/orders/urls.ts
import { SimpleRouter } from 'tvine'
import { OrderViewSet } from './views.ts'
export const appName = 'orders'
export const urlpatterns = new SimpleRouter().register('orders', OrderViewSet).urls
// /orders/ GET POST (orders:order-list), /orders/<int:id>/ GET PUT PATCH DELETE (orders:order-detail)
```

## Gotchas

- No leading `/` in a route: `path('/api/', …)` fails at boot.
- `urls.ts` calls need `x-tvine-api: 1` just like `/tvine/api`; without it every call is `403`.
- `GET` reaches only `readOnly` actions. Use `methods: ['POST']` for writes.
- Path values win only if the body agrees; sending a different `id` in the body is a `400`.
- `include('x.urls')` needs `x` in `apps/` (or installed) and an `apps/x/urls.ts`.
- `re_path` routes are not reversible.
- Routes are read once at boot; a change needs a restart (`tvine dev` reloads).

## See also

[views.md](./views.md) · [actions.md](./actions.md) · [errors.md](./errors.md) · [request.md](./request.md) ·
[settings.md](./settings.md) · [overview.md](./overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/middleware.md

# Middleware

Tvine has two kinds of middleware. **HTTP middleware** wraps every HTTP request
the server answers (pages, `/tvine/api`, `/mcp`, media, `urls.ts` routes), sees the raw Node request on the way
in and the response headers on the way out. You list it in `settings.middleware`; only listed entries run.
**Action middleware** wraps every action call (any transport, including in-process `api.*` and MCP) after
the security checks; it sees the command and can stop it or reshape its events. Hooks (`apps/<app>/hooks.ts`)
only observe.

**Import:** `import { defineMiddleware, MIDDLEWARE_CATALOG, type HttpMiddleware, type MwRequest, type RequestState, type BuildCtx, type Middleware, type Event, Hooks } from 'tvine'`

## HTTP middleware: `settings.middleware`

```ts
middleware: unknown[]   // outermost first
```

Each entry is one of:

| Entry | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| a built-in name | `'tvine.middleware.GZip'` | from the catalog below |
| `[name, options]` | `['tvine.middleware.RateLimit', { limit: 300 }]` | with options |
| a dotted project path | `'config.middleware.timing'` | default export of `config/middleware/timing.ts` (from the project root, `.ts`/`.js`/`.mjs`); missing file or no default export → boot error |
| an object | `defineMiddleware({ name, ... })` | inline |
| a class | `class Timing { constructor(opts, build) {…} processRequest(req, res) {…} }` | built with `(options, BuildCtx)`; its `name` is the class name |
| `[object \| class \| path, options]` | `['config.middleware.timing', { slowMs: 500 }]` | options go to the class constructor |

Default (when you leave `middleware` out): `RequestId`, `AllowedHosts`, `Security`, `Cors`, `GZip`.
`middleware: []` turns all of them off, security headers included. Order is the list order, except
`AllowedHosts`, which is always moved to the front. `tvine check` prints the order it will use.

Plain functions in `settings.middleware` (the old form) are moved to `actionMiddleware`; a list of only
functions keeps the default HTTP list.

`settings.admin.allowIps` appends `['tvine.middleware.IpFilter', { paths: [admin.path], allow: allowIps }]`.

## Built-in catalog

| Name | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `RequestId` | on | Takes a safe `x-request-id` (`[\w.-]{1,128}`) or the `traceparent` trace id, else a new one; sets `req.tvine.id`, adds it to every log line, echoes `x-request-id`. |
| `AllowedHosts` | on | Unknown `Host` (or trusted `X-Forwarded-Host`) → `400 Bad Request (invalid host)`. A direct loopback request (no proxy headers, `trustProxy` 0) always passes. Dev + debug: localhost, LAN IPs, the hostname, `dev.allowedHosts`, `TVINE_DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS` are added, and the 400 names the line to add. No `Host` passes outside production. |
| `Security` | on | Security headers from `settings.security.headers` (CSP with a per-response nonce, HSTS on https, COOP, CORP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy). Sets `req.tvine.cspNonce`. |
| `Cors` | on | Applies `settings.cors`: answers preflights, adds allow headers for allowed origins, `Vary: Origin`; only on paths this server answers. |
| `GZip` | on | Turns on gzip / brotli per `settings.compression`. |
| `SslRedirect` | off | Plain http → `301` to `https://<host><url>` (https read through `trustProxy`). |
| `ConditionalGet` | off | `GET`/`HEAD` 200 with an `ETag` matching `If-None-Match` → `304`. |
| `RateLimit` | off | Per-IP token bucket on every path → `429` + `Retry-After`. Uses `settings.limits.backend`. |
| `IpFilter` | off | Allow / deny by address or CIDR → `403`. Bad CIDR → boot error. Unparseable client IP never matches `allow`. |
| `Maintenance` | off | `503` + `Retry-After` while on (HTML for `Accept: text/html`, else JSON `{ error: 'maintenance', message }`). |
| `BodyLimit` | off | `Content-Length` over the cap → `413`. |
| `Timeout` | off | No response started within `ms` → `503`. Never cuts a response already started. Exempt: `/tvine/channel`, `/tvine/tab`, `/mcp`, the media route. |
| `AccessLog` | off | One `info` line per request on `tvine.request`: method, path (never the query), status, ms, ip, `aborted`. |
| `Locale` | off | `Accept-Language` → `request.locale` (one of `languages`); `Content-Language` + `Vary: Accept-Language` out. |
| `ServerTiming` | off | `Server-Timing: app;dur=<ms>`, only when `settings.debug`. |
| `Shield` | off | `tvine.shield` bot protection (needs `'tvine.shield'` in `installedApps`). Options are Shield's; see its docs. |
| `BotGuard` | off | Known scanner user agents → `403`. Never on the agent surface (`/mcp`, `/tvine/*`, `/.well-known/*`, `/llms.txt`, `*/agent.json|txt`). |

### Options

| Middleware | Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowedHosts` | `hosts` | `string[]` | `settings.allowedHosts` | Replaces the host list. `'*'`, `'.example.com'` (with subdomains), `'*.example.com'`, exact, `[ipv6]`. |
| `SslRedirect` | `exempt` | `string[]` | — | Path prefixes not redirected. |
| | `host` | `string` | the request host | Redirect target host. |
| `RateLimit` | `limit` | `number` | `5 × settings.limits.rate.limit` (300) | Requests per window per IP. |
| | `windowMs` | `number` | `settings.limits.rate.windowMs` (60 000) | Window. |
| | `exempt` | `string[]` | — | Path prefixes not counted. |
| `IpFilter` | `allow` | `string[]` | unset (everyone) | Only these addresses / CIDRs pass. |
| | `deny` | `string[]` | `[]` | These are refused. |
| | `paths` | `string[]` | unset (every path) | Only apply under these prefixes. List the middleware twice for two rules. |
| `Maintenance` | `enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | On. |
| | `file` | `string` | — | On while this file exists. |
| | `retryAfter` | `number` (s) | `300` | `Retry-After`. |
| | `allowIps` | `string[]` | `[]` | Pass through. |
| | `allowPaths` | `string[]` | — | Path prefixes that pass. |
| | `allowStaff` | `boolean` | `false` | A signed-in staff user (session cookie) passes. |
| | `message` | `string` | `'Down for maintenance; back soon.'` | Body text. |
| `BodyLimit` | `maxBytes` | `number` | `settings.limits.bodyBytes` | Cap. |
| | `paths` | `Record<string, number>` | `{}` | Per-prefix caps; the longest matching prefix wins. |
| `Timeout` | `ms` | `number` | `settings.limits.handlerMs + 5000` | Limit. |
| | `exempt` | `string[]` | — | More exempt prefixes. |
| `Locale` | `languages` | `string[]` | `['en']` | Supported tags. |
| | `default` | `string` | first of `languages` | Fallback. |
| `BotGuard` | `block` | `RegExp` | sqlmap, nikto, masscan, nmap, nuclei, wpscan, gobuster, ffuf, … | User-agent pattern. |

Path prefixes match the exact path or anything under `prefix/`. Paths are normalized first (decoded, `\` → `/`,
dot segments and duplicate slashes collapsed), so `/x/../admin` cannot step around a rule.

## Writing HTTP middleware

```ts
interface HttpMiddleware {
  name: string
  process?(req: MwRequest, res: ServerResponse, next: () => Promise<void>): void | Promise<void>
  processRequest?(req: MwRequest, res: ServerResponse): void | Promise<void>
  processResponse?(req: MwRequest, res: ServerResponse): void
  processException?(req: MwRequest, res: ServerResponse, err: unknown): boolean | void | Promise<boolean | void>
}
const defineMiddleware: (m: HttpMiddleware) => HttpMiddleware
```

| Method | When | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `process(req, res, next)` | around (Koa style) | `await next()` resolves when the response finished or the client left. `next()` twice throws. Not together with `processRequest`. |
| `processRequest(req, res)` | on the way in | End the response (`res.writeHead(...).end()`) to stop: inner middleware and transports never run. |
| `processResponse(req, res)` | right before the status line and headers go out, innermost first | Sync. Set or remove headers here. |
| `processException(req, res, err)` | an error thrown by this or an inner middleware | Return `true` if you answered; else the next outer one tries; then `500`. |

`defineMiddleware` throws without a `name` or without at least one method, or with both `process` and `processRequest`.

### `req.tvine` (`RequestState`)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` | Normalized path, no query. |
| `ip` | `string` | Client IP per `settings.trustProxy`. |
| `https` | `boolean` | Per `trustProxy` (`X-Forwarded-Proto`). |
| `host` | `string?` | The validated host (set by `AllowedHosts`), lowercase, no port. |
| `id` | `string?` | Request id (set by `RequestId`). |
| `locale` | `string?` | Set by `Locale`. |
| `start` | `number` | `performance.now()` at arrival. |
| `ours` | `boolean` | `false` in embedded mode for paths the host app answers (middleware is skipped there). |
| `compression` | settings or `false` | Set by `GZip`. |
| `onHeaders(fn)` | function | Run `fn` right before headers are sent. |
| `log` | `Logger` | `tvine.request`, bound to the request id. |
| `verifiedAgent` | `{ directory, keyid }?` | Set by `Shield` for a valid Web Bot Auth signature. |
| `cspNonce` | `string?` | Set by `Security`. |
| `shield` | `unknown` | Shield's signals and decision. |

### `BuildCtx` (class constructors get it as the 2nd argument)

`{ settings, debug, production, sec, cors, userOf? }`: `userOf(req)` resolves the session user from the cookie.

WebSocket upgrades (Next HMR) pass through `AllowedHosts` and `IpFilter` only.

## Action middleware

```ts
type Middleware = (cmd: Command, ctx: ActionCtx, next: () => AsyncIterable<Event>) => AsyncIterable<Event>
```

| Where | Scope |
|---|---|
| `settings.actionMiddleware: Middleware[]` | every action, runs first (outermost) |
| `apps/<app>/middleware.ts` with `export default [fn, ...]` | only that app's actions; default export must be an array of functions (boot error otherwise) |

| Point | Detail |
|---|---|
| Position | After origin check, rate limits, session, `humanOnly`, permissions, bind, rev. Before param validation, `confirm`, the handler and the commit. |
| `cmd` | `{ action, params, sid?, bind?, cmdId?, rev?, agentCmd? }`, deep-frozen (params cannot drift from the idempotency hash). |
| Stop | `yield` an `err` event (`{ kind: 'err', code: 'domain', message, reason? }`) and return without `next()`. |
| Continue | `yield* next()`. Events: `ok`, `snapshot`, `goto`, `err`. |
| Time | Capped at `settings.limits.handlerMs` (the clock pauses while the handler runs). Over it → `internal` "middleware timeout". |
| After commit | Throwing after a committed result, or dropping it, is logged and the committed result is returned anyway. Writes to `ctx` after `next()` are outside the transaction. |

## Hooks (observe only)

`apps/<app>/hooks.ts`: each exported function named after a hook is registered at boot. Any other exported
function name is a boot error.

| Name | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | `{ cmd, action, status, sid, events, ms }` | every action call, after it settled (params redacted, `secretResult` blanked, frozen) |
| `error` | `{ cmd, code, message }` | additionally, on an err outcome |
| `session` | `{ sid, kind: 'created' \| 'expired' }` | session lifecycle |
| `read` | `{ page, via: 'http' \| 'mcp', sid, rev, ms }` | an agent read a page snapshot |
| `ready(server)` | the `ServerCtx` | at boot, awaited, before serving |
| `postMigrate(e)` | `{ app, models, applied }` | after `tvine migrate` |

Also `server.ctx.hooks.on(name, fn)` at run time. Hooks are fire-and-forget; a throw is logged.

## Examples

### 1. Turn on extra built-ins

```ts
// config/settings/base.ts
middleware: [
  'tvine.middleware.RequestId', 'tvine.middleware.AllowedHosts', 'tvine.middleware.Security',
  'tvine.middleware.Cors', 'tvine.middleware.GZip',
  ['tvine.middleware.RateLimit', { limit: 600, exempt: ['/_next/'] }],
  ['tvine.middleware.IpFilter', { allow: ['10.0.0.0/8'], paths: ['/admin'] }],
  ['tvine.middleware.Maintenance', { file: './MAINTENANCE', allowStaff: true }],
  'tvine.middleware.AccessLog',
],
```

### 2. Project middleware by dotted path

```ts
// config/middleware/timing.ts
import { defineMiddleware } from 'tvine'

export default defineMiddleware({
  name: 'timing',
  async process(req, res, next) {
    req.tvine.onHeaders(() => res.setHeader('x-took-ms', (performance.now() - req.tvine.start).toFixed(1)))
    await next()
  },
})
// settings: middleware: [...defaults, 'config.middleware.timing']
```

### 3. A partners-only path with processRequest

```ts
export default defineMiddleware({
  name: 'wholesaleOnly',
  processRequest(req, res) {
    if (req.tvine.path.startsWith('/wholesale') && !req.headers['x-partner-key']) {
      res.writeHead(403, { 'content-type': 'text/plain' }).end('partners only')
    }
  },
})
```

### 4. Action middleware: "shop closed" switch

```ts
// apps/orders/middleware.ts
import type { Middleware } from 'tvine'

const shopClosed: Middleware = async function* (cmd, ctx, next) {
  if (cmd.action === 'orders.place' && ctx.settings.site.name.endsWith('(closed)')) {
    yield { kind: 'err', code: 'domain', reason: 'closed', message: 'The shop is closed today' }
    return
  }
  yield* next()
}
export default [shopClosed]
```

### 5. A hook that logs slow actions

```ts
// apps/orders/hooks.ts
import { getLogger } from 'tvine'
const log = getLogger('orders')
export function command(e: { action: string; status: string; ms: number }) {
  if (e.ms > 1000) log.warn('slow action', { action: e.action, status: e.status, ms: e.ms })
}
```

## Gotchas

- Only listed HTTP middleware runs. Setting `middleware` replaces the defaults: copy the five you want to keep.
- `AllowedHosts` always runs first, whatever its position.
- In production with `AllowedHosts` on and `allowedHosts` empty, boot fails.
- `tvine.middleware.Shield` without `'tvine.shield'` installed fails settings validation.
- Action middleware cannot skip permissions or `humanOnly`: they ran before it.
- `processResponse` is sync and runs at header time; do not await in it.
- A dotted path is resolved from the current working directory (the project root), not from the settings file.

## See also

[settings.md](./settings.md) · [actions.md](./actions.md) · [request.md](./request.md) · [errors.md](./errors.md) ·
[overview.md](./overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/request.md

# Request, sessions, agents and uploads

Every action call gets one `Request` object (`ctx.request`), built by the transport that received the call:
the HTTP page transport, `/tvine/api`, a `urls.ts` route, MCP, the in-process `api.*` of a server component, or
the human `<Form>` path. It is read-only data about the caller: path, query, headers, IP, user, whether an AI
agent is calling, locale, uploaded files. Next to it sits the `Session` (`ctx.session`): Warp's own per-visitor
state, found by a sid (agents) or a cookie (browsers). This page also covers how agents are detected and how
file uploads work.

**Import:** `import { currentRequest, currentSession, cycleSession, defineUpload, media, ANONYMOUS, type Request, type Session, type TvineUser, type UploadedFile } from 'tvine'`

## `Request`

```ts
interface Request {
  method: 'GET' | 'POST'
  path: string
  route: string
  params: Record<string, string>
  query: URLSearchParams
  headers: ReadonlyHeaders          // get(name): string | null
  ip: string
  id: string
  locale?: string
  agent: { is: boolean; via: 'http' | 'mcp' | 'webmcp' | 'channel' | 'inspector' | 'human'; client?: string;
           verified?: { directory: string; keyid: string } }
  files: UploadedFile[]
  user: TvineUser
  raw?: IncomingMessage
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `'GET' \| 'POST'` | `GET` only for an HTTP `GET`; everything else (POST, MCP, `/tvine/api`, in-process) is `POST`. |
| `path` | `string` | The page path. For `/tvine/api` and `urls.ts` calls from a browser it is the **calling page** (the `Referer` path, `/` if none), not the API URL. |
| `route` | `string` | The Next route pattern of `path` (`'/product/[id]'`), or the path when it is not a page. |
| `params` | `Record<string, string>` | Route params from the pattern (`{ id: '42' }`); `[...slug]` joined with `/`. |
| `query` | `URLSearchParams` | The page URL's query. |
| `headers` | `{ get(name) }` | Read-only, case-insensitive. On `/tvine/api` the `x-tvine-*` headers are removed. Over MCP the `cookie` header is removed. |
| `ip` | `string` | Client IP. `X-Forwarded-For` walked right-to-left exactly `settings.trustProxy` hops; never the raw header. Ports, brackets and `::ffff:` removed. |
| `id` | `string` | Request id: a safe incoming `x-request-id`, else the `traceparent` trace id, else a new id. |
| `locale` | `string?` | Set only by the `Locale` middleware (a client-sent `x-tvine-locale` is deleted). |
| `agent` | object | Who is calling, below. |
| `files` | `UploadedFile[]` | Files from a multipart agent POST; empty otherwise. |
| `user` | `TvineUser` | Always present; `ANONYMOUS` when signed out. |
| `raw` | `IncomingMessage?` | The Node request, only on the HTTP page transport and browser `/tvine/api` / `urls.ts` calls. Escape hatch. |

### `TvineUser`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `isAuthenticated` | `boolean` | Signed in. |
| `isAnonymous` | `boolean?` | `true` on `ANONYMOUS`. |
| `id`, `name` | `string?` | From the auth backend. |
| `claims` | `Record<string, unknown>?` | Whatever a BYO resolver returns. |
| `isActive`, `isStaff`, `isSuperuser` | `boolean?` | Filled by `tvine.auth`. |
| `scopes` | `string[]?` | Token-authenticated: `'*'`, `'read'`, `'app.*'`, `'app.x'`. Dispatch refuses actions outside them. |
| `hasPerm(perm, obj?)` | `Promise<boolean>?` | Is one permission (`'app.codename'`) granted, optionally for `obj`. |

Resolution order: `settings.auth.user(request)` (BYO, wins) → a bearer token (`tvine.auth`) → the session's user.
Details: [contrib/auth.md](./contrib/auth.md).

## How agents are detected (`request.agent`)

| Path in | `agent.is` | `via` | `client` |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP page URL with the `settings.header` header (default `x-tvine`, any value) | `true` | `'http'` | `User-Agent` |
| HTTP page URL with `Accept` containing `text/tvine`, `application/tvine+json`, or `text/markdown` ranked at least as high as `text/html` | `true` | `'http'` | `User-Agent` |
| `GET <page>/agent.json` (always) or `<page>/agent.txt` (when `formats.notationPath`) | `true` | `'http'` | `User-Agent` |
| HTTP page URL, none of the above | not an agent: the request goes to Next | — | — |
| `/tvine/api` or a `urls.ts` route with the same header / `Accept` markers | `true` | `'http'` | `User-Agent` |
| `/tvine/api` / `urls.ts` without them | `false` | `'human'` | `User-Agent` |
| MCP (`POST /mcp`) | `true` | `'mcp'` | MCP `clientInfo.name` |
| A bearer API token (`Authorization`, `tvine.auth`) | `true` | unchanged | unchanged |
| Body `agentCmd: { via: 'webmcp' }` (in-browser agent) | `true` | `'webmcp'` | unchanged |
| Body `agentCmd` with any other `via` | `true` | `'channel'` (`'inspector'` only when `settings.debug`) | unchanged |
| Any request of a session whose tab a remote agent controls right now | `true` | `'channel'` | unchanged |
| Next server forward (two-server mode) flagged agent, or an agent's snapshot render | `true` | `'http'` | — |
| `verified` | set only by `tvine.middleware.Shield` for a valid Web Bot Auth signature, never from a header | | |

The flag is **downgrade-only**: a client can mark a request as an agent, never as a human. `denyAgents`,
`humanOnly`, MCP hiding and `confirm.by: 'human'` all read `request.agent.is`.

## Sessions

```ts
interface Session {
  sid: Sid                       // 21-char id
  rev: Rev                       // +1 per committed non-readOnly action
  data: Map<string, unknown>     // your state: cart, wizard step, …
  createdAt: number; lastSeen: number
  controller?: string            // reserved
}
```

| Topic | Rule |
|---|---|
| Found by | `sid` (agents: `x-tvine-sid` header, `?sid=` on GET, body `sid`, MCP `sid` arg) or the session cookie (browsers). |
| Created | On an agent page GET without one; on a write through `/tvine/api` (the cookie is set in the reply); never by a page view. A read without a session runs on a throwaway session that is not stored. |
| `data` in actions | The handler works on a deep copy; it replaces the real data only after the action succeeds. A `readOnly` action may write `data` too (saved, no rev bump). |
| One at a time | Commands of one sid run one after another (queue depth 16, then `rate_limited`); with redis also across servers. |
| Idle expiry | `settings.session.ttlMs` (24 h) since `lastSeen`. |
| Absolute expiry | `settings.session.maxAgeMs` (14 days) since `createdAt`; `0` = none. |
| Cap | `settings.session.max` (100 000) live sessions per process; least recently used evicted. |
| Store | `settings.session.backend`: `'memory'` (per process) or `'redis'`. |
| Expired / unknown sid on a command | `expired_sid` with a fresh sid + snapshot attached. |
| Rotation | `cycleSession(ctx)` in a handler: after commit the session gets a new sid; the old sid and its cookies stop working (login, logout). |

### The session cookie

`<cookieName>=<value>; Path=/; Max-Age=<ttlMs/1000>; HttpOnly; SameSite=<Lax|Strict|None>[; Secure]`

| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `session.cookieName` | `tvine_s` | Becomes `__Host-tvine_s` when `secure` is on. |
| `session.secure` | on in production (`TVINE_SESSION_SECURE`) | `Secure` flag. |
| `session.sameSite` | `'lax'` | `'none'` needs `secure`. |

The cookie value is not the sid; the sid is never written into a response body for a cookie-only browser.
A sid named by the caller (`?sid=`, header, body) never becomes a browser cookie. App cookies (other than the
session): Not covered by Warp; read `request.headers.get('cookie')` or use Next's `cookies()`.

### In server components

```ts
const currentSession: () => Promise<Session | undefined>   // the page's session, undefined if none
const currentRequest: () => Promise<Request>               // the page's Request (user, agent, ip, …)
```

They read the cookie (or, during an agent's snapshot render, that agent's session). They throw when no tvine
server runs in the process or the page is being prerendered at build: make the page dynamic
(`await connection()`). Reading the session marks the agent snapshot as personal (never shared-cached).

## Uploads

```ts
function defineUpload(name: string, opts: {
  maxBytes: number; types: string[]
  storage?: Storage; permissions?: Permission[]; uploadTo?: string
  public?: boolean; private?: boolean
  rate?: { limit: number; windowMs: number }
}): UploadDef                                             // an ordinary action; export it from views.ts
```

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxBytes` | `number` | required | File size cap → `too_large` (HTTP 413). |
| `types` | `string[]` | required | Allowed MIME types, checked by sniffing the first bytes (not the client's type). Known: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `application/pdf`. Else `unsupported_type`. |
| `storage` | `Storage` | `DiskStorage(settings.media.dir, settings.media.route)` | Where files go. |
| `permissions` | `Permission[]` | `[]` | Action permissions. |
| `uploadTo` | `string` | — | Key folder: `'avatars'` → `avatars/<id>.png`. Folder names joined by `/`. |
| `public` | `boolean` | `false` | Served with `Cache-Control: public`. |
| `private` | `boolean` | `false` | Only via a signed, expiring URL (`media.url`). Not with `public`. |
| `rate` | rate | 5 per minute | The 5/min default yields to `apps/<app>/rules.ts`; an explicit `rate` beats both. |

The action's param is `file`; the result is an `UploadedFile`:
`{ field: 'file', key, url, type, size }` (for a private file `url` is signed for 1 h).

Ways to send the file:

| Transport | How |
|---|---|
| Agent HTTP (page URL, `x-tvine: 1`) | `multipart/form-data`: text fields `action` (must come before the file), optional `sid`, `cmdId`, `bind`, `rev`; then exactly one file part named `file`; nothing after it. Streamed to storage; removed again if the action fails. |
| JSON (`api.*`, `/tvine/api`, MCP) | `params: { file: { base64: '…' } }`, max 256 KB decoded. URLs are refused. |

`media.url(key, { expiresIn?: seconds (3600), user? })` signs a private-file URL; `user` limits it to that user.

`/tvine/api` also accepts `multipart/form-data` (a `params` JSON part + file parts) for actions that declare
`multipart: { maxBytes, partBytes? }` on the def (the admin uses it); only for a signed-in, same-origin caller.
App-level use of that path: Not covered.

## Examples

### 1. Read the caller in an action

```ts
import { z } from 'zod'
import { defineAction, DomainError, getLogger } from 'tvine'

export const checkout = defineAction('checkout', z.object({}), async (_p, ctx) => {
  const { user, agent, ip } = ctx.request
  if (!user.isAuthenticated) throw new DomainError('forbidden', 'sign in to check out')
  getLogger('orders').info('checkout', { user: user.id, agent: agent.is ? agent.client : 'human', ip })
  return { cart: ctx.session.data.get('cart') ?? {} }
})
```

### 2. A page that shows the cart from the session

```tsx
// app/cart/page.tsx
import { connection } from 'next/server'
import { currentSession } from 'tvine'

export default async function Cart() {
  await connection()
  const s = await currentSession()
  const cart = (s?.data.get('cart') as Record<number, number> | undefined) ?? {}
  return <p>{Object.keys(cart).length} items</p>
}
```

### 3. Product image upload

```ts
// apps/catalog/views.ts
import { defineUpload, isStaff } from 'tvine'
export const uploadImage = defineUpload('uploadImage', {
  maxBytes: 2_000_000, types: ['image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/webp'],
  uploadTo: 'products', public: true, permissions: [isStaff],
})   // → catalog.uploadImage
```

```bash
# POST to any routed page (here /sell); the action field comes first
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/sell -H 'x-tvine: 1' \
  -F action=catalog.uploadImage -F sid=$SID -F file=@hat.png
```

### 4. Agent request with an explicit sid

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3000/shop -H 'x-tvine: 1' -H "x-tvine-sid: $SID"
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/shop -H 'x-tvine: 1' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"action\":\"cart.addToCart\",\"params\":{\"productId\":7,\"qty\":1},\"sid\":\"$SID\",\"cmdId\":\"c1\"}"
```

## Gotchas

- `request.path` on an API call is the page that made the call, so `settings.guards` apply by page.
- `request.ip` is the socket address unless `settings.trustProxy` is set; behind a proxy set it, or every
  client shares one rate-limit key.
- `request.user` is resolved lazily from the session; inside an action it is final.
- A page view never creates a session (pages cannot set cookies); the first write does.
- `x-tvine` on `/tvine/api` makes the call an agent call (`humanOnly` refuses it).
- Upload type checks sniff bytes; a renamed `.exe` as `image/png` is refused.
- The multipart upload path needs the `action` field before the `file` part.

## See also

[actions.md](./actions.md) · [middleware.md](./middleware.md) · [errors.md](./errors.md) · [settings.md](./settings.md) ·
[contrib/auth.md](./contrib/auth.md) · [overview.md](./overview.md)


# docs/reference/warp/errors.md

# Errors

Every action call ends in exactly one outcome: `ok`, `goto`, or `err`. An `err` carries a fixed `code` (one of
eleven), a `message`, and optionally a `reason` (your `DomainError` code), the bad `field`, every bad field in
`errors[]`, `retryAfterMs`, or a `confirm` ask. Handlers report business failures by throwing `DomainError`;
Warp maps everything else (validation, permissions, limits, stale state, crashes) itself. The same `err` reaches
every caller: as an `ApiResult` for `api.*` / `/tvine/api` / `urls.ts`, as a snapshot envelope for agents over
HTTP, as an MCP tool result with `isError: true`. Agent-facing text also gets a fixed recovery hint.

**Import:** `import { DomainError, type ErrCode, type FieldError } from 'tvine'` (client side: `ApiError`, `must`
from `tvine/api`)

## `DomainError`

```ts
class DomainError extends Error {
  constructor(code: string, message: string, field?: string, errors?: FieldError[])
  code: string; field?: string; errors?: FieldError[]
}
interface FieldError { field: string; code?: string; message: string }
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | Your machine-readable reason (`'out_of_stock'`, `'not_found'`, `'forbidden'`). |
| `message` | Shown to the user / agent. Write it as the business rule. |
| `field` | The param at fault (forms highlight it). |
| `errors` | Several bad fields at once. |

How a thrown `DomainError` becomes an `err`:

| `code` you throw | `err.code` | `err.reason` | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| `'invalid_param'` | `invalid_param` | `'invalid_param'` | 400 |
| `'internal'` | `internal` | `'internal'` | 500 |
| `'human_only'` | `human_only` | `'human_only'` | 403 |
| `'forbidden'` | `domain` | `'forbidden'` | 403 |
| `'not_found'` | `domain` | `'not_found'` | 404 |
| anything else | `domain` | your code | 400 |

Any other thrown error → `internal`, message `"internal error"` (details only in the `tvine` log). The
transaction rolls back in every error case.

## Error codes (`ErrCode`)

| Code | When | Recovery hint (appended for agents) |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_param` | zod validation failed; unknown or read-only param; a `bind` key sent as a param; bad body / Content-Type; body too large (`reason: 'too_large'`) | fix the field named in the error to match the expected type; see the action spec in the snapshot |
| `unknown_action` | no action with that id (or MCP-disabled over MCP) | use one of the valid actions listed for this page |
| `stale_bind` | `bind` missing (action has `rules.bind`), invalid, expired, or issued for another action | re-read the page and use its fresh action refs |
| `stale_rev` | `rev` given and not the session's current rev (fresh snapshot attached) | state changed; a fresh snapshot is attached, retry against it |
| `expired_sid` | no session / unknown / expired / rotated sid (new sid + snapshot attached when one was created) | a new sid is in the attached snapshot envelope; use it from now on |
| `rate_limited` | a rate bucket is empty; a sid's queue is full; the session is busy on another server (`retryAfterMs` set) | retry after the delay shown |
| `conflict` | the same `cmdId` reused with different params | command already executed with different params; use a new cmdId for new params |
| `domain` | a `DomainError` with your code (in `reason`); permission denied / cross-origin / guarded route (`reason: 'forbidden'`) | the message above is the business rule; change the input or choose another option (forbidden: not allowed for this session; do not retry it, choose another page or action) |
| `internal` | uncaught error, handler timeout, middleware timeout, failed session rotation | server error; retry once, then re-read the page |
| `human_only` | an agent-marked request hit a `humanOnly` action, a `humanOnly` field, or a `confirm.by: 'human'` | only a human can do this; ask the user to do it themselves, do not retry |
| `confirm_required` | a `rules.confirm` action's first call: nothing ran | nothing ran: confirm as the message says (with the token), or ask the user when only they can confirm |

### Reasons you will see

| `reason` | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `forbidden` | `domain` | Permission denied, token scope, cross-origin, guarded route, off-site redirect. |
| `not_found` | `domain` | A missing object (class views, your `DomainError('not_found')`). |
| `render_mutation` | `domain` | A non-`readOnly` action was called during a page render. |
| `too_large` | `invalid_param` / `domain` | Body or file over its limit. |
| `unsupported_type` | `domain` | Upload type not in `types`. |
| `confirm_required` | `confirm_required` | The first call of a confirmed action. |
| `confirm_invalid` | `domain` | Bad, expired, reused token, or params changed since the confirm. |
| `human_only` | `human_only` | See above. |
| `two_factor_required`, `reauth_required` | `domain` | A permission refused with these (kept as reason). |
| `cancelled` | `confirm_required` | Client side: the human pressed Cancel on the confirm dialog. |
| `network` | `internal` | Client side: `fetch` failed. |

## `confirm_required`

The first call of an action with `rules.confirm` runs nothing and answers:

```ts
{ ok: false, code: 'confirm_required', reason: 'confirm_required', message: 'Refund order 42? — …',
  confirm: { token?: string, message: string, summary: Record<string, unknown>, expiresIn: 120, by: 'anyone' | 'human' } }
```

Call again with the same params plus `$confirm: token` (in `params`) within 120 s, once. `summary` is the params
with secrets redacted and long values cut to 200 chars. With `by: 'human'` an agent gets no token, and an agent
sending one gets `human_only`. In the browser, `api.*` shows a dialog and resends automatically.

## `goto` (redirects)

| Where | What happens |
|---|---|
| Handler calls Next's `redirect(url)` | The action commits, the outcome is `goto`. The URL must be http(s), on this site's host, and a routed page; else `domain` / `forbidden` (and a rollback). A non-URL target is `internal`. |
| An agent reads a page whose render redirects | The agent gets `goto <url>` instead of a snapshot. |
| `api.*` | `{ ok: true, data, goto }`. |

## Not found

| Where | Do |
|---|---|
| In an action | `throw new DomainError('not_found', 'product 7 not found', 'id')` → 404 on `/tvine/api`. |
| In a page | Next's `notFound()`. For an agent this becomes `domain` / `not_found` (HTTP 404). |
| From `api.*` in a page | `must(await api.catalog.get({ id }), { notFound: true })` throws Next's 404 for `reason: 'not_found'`. |
| Class view helper | `await ProductDetail.object(id)` returns `undefined` for not found / forbidden. |

## Field errors

Validation lists every bad field:

```json
{ "ok": false, "code": "invalid_param", "field": "qty",
  "message": "qty: Number must be greater than or equal to 1; color: Required",
  "errors": [ { "field": "qty", "code": "too_small", "message": "Number must be greater than or equal to 1" },
              { "field": "color", "code": "invalid_type", "message": "Required" } ] }
```

`field` is the first bad field. Nested paths are put in the message (`"address: city: Required"`). Unknown keys
get code `unknown`, read-only ones `read_only`. The human `<Form>` turns them into `{ [field]: message }`.

## HTTP status codes

| Code | `/tvine/api`, `urls.ts` | Agent HTTP (page URL) |
|---|---|---|
| ok | 200 (201 for a generated `create` via `urls.ts`) | 200 (304 on `If-None-Match` for GET) |
| `invalid_param` | 400 (413 body too large) | 400 (413 body too large) |
| `unknown_action` | 404 | 400 |
| `stale_bind`, `stale_rev`, `conflict`, `confirm_required` | 400 | 400 |
| `expired_sid` | 401 | 401 |
| `rate_limited` | 429 (`retryAfterMs` in the body) | 429 + `Retry-After` header |
| `domain` | 403 (`forbidden`), 404 (`not_found`), else 400 | same |
| `human_only` | 403 | 403 |
| `internal` | 500 | 500 |
| no `x-tvine-api: 1` / bad forward | 403 (`domain`, `forbidden`) | — |
| wrong method | 405 + `Allow` | humans' requests pass to Next |
| not a page | — | 404 (`domain`) |

HTTP middleware answers with plain text: 400 (bad host), 403 (IpFilter, BotGuard), 413, 429, 503 (Maintenance,
Timeout).

## Over MCP

A tool result is `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text }], isError: true }` for any `err`. The text is the rendered
envelope (`settings.formats.default`: JSON or notation) including the recovery hint and, for
`confirm_required`, the token. A thrown error inside a tool is never passed through as a JSON-RPC error; it
becomes `internal`. Tab-control errors carry reasons like `awaiting_approval`, `not_connected`, `human_denied`,
`busy`, `timeout`, `tab_closed`.

## On the client (`tvine/api`)

`api.*` never throws; check `r.ok`. `must(r)` returns `r.data` or throws `ApiError` (`code`, `reason`, `field`,
`errors`, `message`).

## Examples

### 1. A business rule

```ts
export const place = defineAction('place', z.object({ productId: z.number().int(), qty: z.number().int().min(1) }),
  async ({ productId, qty }) => {
    const p = await Product.objects.filter({ id: productId }).first()
    if (!p) throw new DomainError('not_found', `product ${productId} not found`, 'productId')
    if (p.stock < qty) throw new DomainError('out_of_stock', `only ${p.stock} left`, 'qty')
    // …
  })
// → { ok: false, code: 'domain', reason: 'out_of_stock', field: 'qty', message: 'only 2 left' }  (HTTP 400)
```

### 2. Several field errors at once

```ts
throw new DomainError('invalid_param', 'address is incomplete', 'zip', [
  { field: 'zip', message: 'unknown zip code' },
  { field: 'city', message: 'does not match the zip' },
])
```

### 3. Handling results in a client component

```tsx
const r = await api.orders.place({ productId: 7, qty: 3 })
if (r.ok) router.push(r.goto ?? '/orders')
else if (r.code === 'rate_limited') setError(`Try again in ${Math.ceil((r.retryAfterMs ?? 1000) / 1000)} s`)
else if (r.reason === 'out_of_stock') setError(r.message)
else for (const e of r.errors ?? []) setFieldError(e.field, e.message)
```

### 4. Object permission denial in a view

```ts
async checkObjectPermissions(ctx, order) {
```
